records.head: # Runbook — committing from the sandbox (lock workaround)
records.text:
# Runbook — committing from the sandbox (lock workaround)

*Why this exists: the sandbox mount runs a **delete-guard** — git can create `.git/*.lock` and
`objects/tmp_obj_*` files but **cannot unlink them** (`rm` → "Operation not permitted", even as the
file's owner). So git commits fail with `Unable to create '.git/index.lock': File exists`, and any git
command leaves a fresh lock behind. `mv` IS permitted where `rm` is not — that's the whole trick.
Companion to memory `git-push-method`; git split = Claude commits; push runs from the terminal via
`bash knowledge/_git_commit.sh --push` **on Dave's explicit word only** (`s133-D2`: master · ff-only ·
verified; keyed by Dave at #141). GitHub Desktop remains legal on his side. *(Summary corrected #187,
W-23 — the pre-#133 "Dave pushes via Desktop" split aged out; body correction at step 5 below.)**

records.head: ★ STEP 0 BEFORE EVERYTHING — ASK FOR THE DELETE GRANT (ruled by Dave #133: "do it")
records.text:
## ★ STEP 0 BEFORE EVERYTHING — ASK FOR THE DELETE GRANT (ruled by Dave #133: "do it")

**The entire lock dance below routes around a permission that is ONE TOOL CALL away.** Call
`mcp__cowork__allow_cowork_file_delete` at the FIRST commit of the session (not in wrap heat).
If granted, `rm` works inside `.git`, git tidies its own locks, and **none of the mv choreography
is needed** — commit normally (identity flags + `-F` msgfile + read the MESSAGE back, those rules
still stand). The mv sequence below is the FALLBACK for a refused/absent grant.
⚠ The grant appears to be PER-SESSION — ask each session, first commit.
★ Why this section exists: #133 fought the delete-guard through an entire wrap (alternate index,
doubled subject, 29 lock husks) while quoting the step-4b text that names the tool — the
"sandbox cannot" premise was true of the DEFAULT state and the procedure was never re-priced
after the tool shipped ([[assertion-propagation-gap]], the same class step 4b's own correction
records). Dave: "that is hilarious that you didn't just ask this in the first place."

records.head: The procedure — RUN THE SCRIPT (2026-07-26, dream-pass P2, Dave ruled)
records.text:
## The procedure — RUN THE SCRIPT (2026-07-26, dream-pass P2, Dave ruled)

```
git status --short                                   # step 0.5 — account for EVERY dirty path first
bash knowledge/_git_commit.sh --reconciled <msgfile>  # clear · stage · clear · commit · clear
```

The script mechanises the whole sequence below, refuses to stage while any `.git/*.lock` exists,
refuses an empty/stale msgfile, verifies HEAD advanced AND the message matches, and clears locks as
its last action. It cannot do step 0.5's judgment — the `--reconciled` flag is your attestation that
every dirty path is accounted for (worktree-reconcile rule). WHY a script: 8 of 10 commit sessions (3 of 5 at ruling 2026-07-26; #36, #41, #56, #109 and #117 since — the count is maintained because it is the evidence for this tool. ⚠ #109 hand-rolled the lock `mv` AND ran a control probe to re-derive the 0-byte/mtime diagnostic already written in Gotchas below, then found the script — Dave caught it with "there s a commit runbook". The memory hook, not the runbook, was the misfire: it carried "ask if GitHub Desktop is open" WITHOUT the diagnostic that answers it. Hook corrected #109. ⚠ #117 RECURRED IT IN A NEW SHAPE AND THE HOOK WAS NOT AT FAULT: memory `git-lock-mv-not-rm` DOES say "RUN `_git_commit.sh`" and #117 DID run it — then, when the script refused on R3 CHAIN OVERTAKEN, improvised two escape-hatch spellings instead of opening this file. ★ **The runbook was consulted only after the SCRIPT surprised me, which is precisely when line 22 says to read it — so the miss was not "forgot the script", it was "treated a refusal as a syntax puzzle".** Dave caught it again, with the same sentence, and that repetition is why this parenthesis keeps growing. ⚠ #133 RECURRED IT IN A THIRD SHAPE: ran the script, hit the lock refusal, and improvised a GIT_INDEX_FILE alternate-index commit (plus a cat-overwrite of .git/index) instead of opening this file — where the manual sequence would have worked: the 'immovable' lock was the documented stale 0-byte signature, and its reappearance after mv was the documented status-respawn. The subject came out T3-double-rewritten and was repaired by the documented amend-from-fresh-msgfile remedy WITHOUT having read it — a right repair by luck is not a read runbook. Dave caught it with the same sentence, third time: "did you use the commit runbook?")
reconstructed this sequence from memory under wrap heat and hit the lock failure first; a hot agent
can call one script (`feedback-gate-dont-patch`). Everything below is the reference the script
implements — read it when the script surprises you, don't re-derive it.

records.head: The manual sequence (reference — the script implements this)
records.text:
## The manual sequence (reference — the script implements this)

**Clear locks BEFORE staging as well as after — the sequence is clear · stage · clear · commit · clear.**
A lock left behind by the *previous* session blocks `git add` itself, so starting at "stage" only works
from an already-clean `.git`. (Corrected 2026-07-18 after step 1 failed on a 12-minute-old stale lock.)

0. **Clear any inherited lock first** (not `rm` — `mv`):
   ```
   cd <repo> && mkdir -p _to_delete/_stale_locks
   for L in $(find .git -name '*.lock'); do mv "$L" _to_delete/_stale_locks/; done
   find .git -name '*.lock'      # expect: none — if not, stop; do not stage
   ```
0.5. **Account for every dirty path BEFORE you stage** (added 2026-07-19). `git add -A` is a blunt
   sweep — it will commit a worker's half-finished experiment or a broken artifact as readily as your
   own work, and a *selective* add silently drops worker dirt. Neither failure is otherwise guarded.
   Reconcile first:
   ```
   git status --short            # every path below must be explained
   ```
   Confirm you can name WHY each dirty path exists (yours, or a known worker's). Any path you can't
   account for → **stop**: `ls notes/_receipts/` and read the sibling sessions
   (`mcp__session_info__list_sessions` → transcript) before committing. This matters most with parallel
   sessions live — the working tree is shared, so their changes are already in yours. Companion:
   `_RUNBOOK-parallel-conductor.md` conductor step 2.5.
1. **Stage** (this may print `unable to unlink … tmp_obj_*` warnings — harmless, ignore):
   ```
   git add -A
   git diff --cached --name-only    # confirm the files actually staged
   ```
   > If this prints *"Another git process seems to be running … remove the file manually"*, a lock
   > survived step 0. Nothing staged. Re-run step 0 and try again — do **not** proceed.
2. **Move every lock aside again** (staging respawns `index.lock`):
   ```
   for L in $(find .git -name '*.lock'); do mv "$L" _to_delete/_stale_locks/; done
   find .git -name '*.lock'      # expect: none
   ```
3. **Commit** with identity set (fresh sandboxes have none). It prints `unable to unlink` warnings but
   **the commit still lands** — verify by the HEAD hash, not the warnings:
   ```
   git -c user.name="Claude" -c user.email="claude@anthropic.com" commit -F <msgfile>
   git log --oneline -1          # confirm the new hash is HEAD — and the MESSAGE is yours
   ```
   ⚠ **Write `<msgfile>` under a dir this session owns (outputs/), with a UNIQUE name, and `head -1`
   it before `-F`.** Never a fixed `/tmp` name — see the 2026-07-22 gotcha below.
   ⛔ **AND THE MSGFILE HEADLINE MUST NOT CARRY A SESSION PREFIX OF ITS OWN** — neither
   `after #N <date> — ` nor `#N <date> — `. **T3 GENERATES the session prefix**, so a headline that
   already has one comes out DOUBLED in `git log`. Observed #185: the subject doubled and had to be
   amended from a fresh msgfile in the same session. Start the headline at the actual subject.
4. **Clear the lock git just re-created**, as the *last* action (any git command, even `status`,
   respawns `index.lock`). Do NOT run another git command after this:
   ```
   for L in $(find .git -name '*.lock'); do mv "$L" _to_delete/_stale_locks/; done
   ```
4b. *(Optional sweep — dream-pass P8, 2026-07-26. ⛔ **CORRECTED #41 — this step used to route the job
   to Dave and that was wrong.**)* If `_to_delete/` is bulging, **the agent clears it — do NOT put it in
   the handoff.** `rm` fails `Operation not permitted` **until permission is granted**, and there is a
   tool for exactly that: **`mcp__cowork__allow_cowork_file_delete`**, whose own description says to call
   it *"whenever a delete operation (such as rm) fails with 'Operation not permitted', rather than
   telling the user it is impossible."* Then `rm -rf _to_delete/*` works. ⚠ **Keep the directory and
   re-`mkdir -p _to_delete/_stale_locks`** — the lock workaround writes there every commit.
   ★ **Why this correction exists:** #41 handed Dave a terminal command; he replied *"i dont know how to
   do this."* He pushes via GitHub Desktop by design and should never need a shell. **A step that routes
   agent-solvable work to the human is a defect in the step** — and this is the THIRD mechanism #41
   hand-rolled around in one window (`_git_commit.sh`, the chain file, this).
5. **Hand off to Dave** — "committed at `<hash>`, locks clear, safe to push." Dave pushes via
   **GitHub Desktop only** (never terminal push — it hangs on credentials).
   ⚠ **CORRECTED #141 (2026-08-10, on Dave's word: "you can push I gave you the rights and the key"):**
   the agent CAN now push from the sandbox — verified live, remote advanced. ★ **The ruled CALL FORM
   is `bash knowledge/_git_commit.sh --push`** (`s133-D2`: *"the ONLY push path"* — master, ff-only,
   verified; exercised #133 and #135), not a raw `git push`. *(Call form added #187, W-23 — the file
   had zero mentions of `--push` while the ledger and the `git-push-method` hook both carried it.)* The
   "hangs on credentials" claim was true of the un-keyed default and aged out once Dave installed a key
   ([[assertion-propagation-gap]], same class as step 4b's correction). **Push still only on Dave's
   explicit word — that half of the split stands.** If Desktop ever complains
   about a lock, Dave can delete `.git/index.lock` on his side (his machine has normal permissions).

records.head: Gotchas
records.text:
## Gotchas
- **Judge success by HEAD, not warnings.** The `unable to unlink … tmp_obj_*` / `*.lock` lines are git
  failing to tidy its own scratch files; the commit object is written and HEAD advances regardless.
- ★ **`git checkout -- <path>` CANNOT RESTORE A FILE ON THIS MOUNT (measured #139).** It fails with
  *"unable to unlink"* — the same permission shape as the `index.lock` wart, because the restore is
  implemented as unlink-then-write and only the unlink is denied. ⚠ **The file is left UNCHANGED, so a
  session that reads the warning as cosmetic (per the first Gotcha above, which is about COMMITS) will
  believe it reverted something it did not.** **The working restore is `git show HEAD:<path> > <path>`**
  — a plain write, no unlink. Same family as the same-mount-`mv`-only rule in `_RUNBOOK-render-verify.md`.
- **Never `rm` inside `.git`** from the sandbox — it fails and wastes a turn. Always `mv` aside.
- **A stale lock is not a live lock.** Before assuming GitHub Desktop is holding it, check: a **0-byte**
  `index.lock` whose mtime is ~the same instant as `.git/index` is the signature of a *completed* git
  operation that then failed to unlink its own lock — i.e. this delete-guard, not a live process.
  Moving that aside is safe. A lock Desktop genuinely holds is a different situation; keep Desktop
  closed during sandbox git work (memory `git-push-method`).
- **The warnings lie about failure, and `git status` lies about success.** Even a read-only
  `git status` respawns `index.lock`, so a clean-looking status run leaves the next `git add` blocked.
  That is why step 4 says the lock-clear must be the *last* git-touching action.
- **`_to_delete/` is gitignored.** ⛔ **CORRECTED #41 — the old text here read *"the bridge can't empty
  it from the sandbox — Dave deletes it on his machine"*, and that is FALSE:** the agent clears it after
  `mcp__cowork__allow_cowork_file_delete` grants the folder (see step 4b). **Never commit `_to_delete/`,
  and never hand the cleanup to Dave.** ⚠ The false claim survived because *"the sandbox cannot"* is TRUE
  of the default state and nobody re-tested it once a permission tool existed — [[assertion-propagation-gap]]:
  the gate fires on a FLIP, so a line that was true when written and quietly went stale is never chased.
- **Big/licensed binaries** (fonts, raw exports) must be gitignored before `git add -A` — check
  `git status --short` for anything under `knowledge/assets/fonts/` or `knowledge/tokens/_raw/`.
- **The stale-msgfile trap (bitten 2026-07-22).** `/tmp` persists across sessions and a file there can
  be OWNED-UNWRITABLE by a later session. Sequence that bit: heredoc to `/tmp/msg.txt` failed
  ("Permission denied") but the command chain continued, and `git commit -F /tmp/msg.txt` silently read
  **yesterday's message from the stale file** — 43 files inscribed under the previous session's text.
  Confident-false-inscription, in git. Caught same minute (`git log -1` showed the wrong headline);
  fixed by `--amend -F` from a fresh uniquely-named file under outputs/. Rules: unique msgfile name in
  a session-owned dir · `head -1` the file before `-F` · after committing, read the MESSAGE back, not
  just the hash. (Amend is safe only while the commit is unpushed — check `git status -sb` ahead-count
  first; if Desktop might be open, confirm the bad commit didn't just get pushed.)
- If commits must be frequent/reliable, re-run the task **"On your computer"** (desktop app → Run
  this task) so the terminal has real unlink permissions and this dance isn't needed.

records.head: Reverting in the sandbox — and the trap in the bulk form (added 2026-07-19, T-D12)
records.text:
## Reverting in the sandbox — and the trap in the bulk form (added 2026-07-19, T-D12)

`git checkout` FAILS here: it needs to unlink, and the `.git` mount blocks unlink. **Write-in-place
is the working revert:**

```bash
git show HEAD:<path> > <path>                                   # one file
for f in $(git diff --name-only); do git show HEAD:$f > $f; done  # everything — SEE WARNING
```

⚠️ **The bulk form reverts YOUR TOOLING TOO.** During T-D12 I used it to reset an experiment and it
silently took `apply_type_bind.py` — the script the experiment depended on — back to HEAD with it.
The next run then produced HEAD's behaviour while I read the output as the new behaviour. Cost:
two wasted render cycles before I noticed.

**Before any bulk revert, park work-in-progress tooling outside the repo:**
```bash
cp knowledge/apply_type_bind.py /tmp/apply_type_bind.py.patched   # park
for f in $(git diff --name-only); do git show HEAD:$f > $f; done  # revert
cp /tmp/apply_type_bind.py.patched knowledge/apply_type_bind.py   # restore the instrument
```
The general rule: **a revert is scoped to the EXPERIMENT, never to the instrument measuring it.**
If the instrument is itself uncommitted, `git diff --name-only` cannot tell them apart — you must.

records.head: Sandbox wart — build kills at call boundaries (banked 2026-07-27 #15)
records.text:
## Sandbox wart — build kills at call boundaries (banked 2026-07-27 #15)

**Nothing survives a tool-call boundary in this sandbox** — `nohup` and `setsid` both get reaped
(tested #15). A `_build_all.py` killed mid-run freezes whatever step was writing: the signature is
**~33 stripped compliance JSONs + `_CAPTURE-GATE.md`** (#14's "34 files / 1,335 deleted lines" and
#15's 33/1,336 were the same event). **Run the build FOREGROUND, ONE call — it fits inside 45s.**
Restore stripped files with `git show HEAD:<path> > <path>` — the delete-guard blocks `git checkout`'s
unlink (`Operation not permitted`), and `git status` itself can strand `index.lock` if its call is
reaped (clear per step 0 above).

{
  "name": "Avatar group",
  "category": "molecule",
  "$status": "PROPOSED #203, Dave's eye owed",
  "purpose": "A set of people shown as one object: overlapping Avatar discs, primary-first, with an overflow counter when the set is longer than the display cap. The unit of meaning is the GROUP ('five people are on this approval'), not the individuals.",
  "$differsFromAvatar": "Avatar (GATED) is the single disc — initials, image or icon, sizes small/medium/large, optionally linking to one profile. Avatar group adds NOTHING to that disc: the disc markup, its surface, its ring and its round exemption are copied verbatim. What it adds is the ARRANGEMENT — negative-margin overlap, a separator ring, a display cap, an overflow counter, and a single accessible name for the whole set. Rule of thumb: one person = Avatar; a countable set of people = Avatar group; a list of people you act on individually = List-items.",
  "props": [
    { "name": "size", "type": "enum", "values": ["small", "medium", "large"], "default": "medium",
      "$note": "32 / 44 / 64 — Avatar's own ramp, copied exactly. Overlap follows at -8 / -12 / -16 (a quarter of the disc), so a member always shows enough of itself to read as a separate person.",
      "$status": "PROPOSED #203, Dave's eye owed" },
    { "name": "max", "type": "number", "default": 3,
      "$note": "Display cap. Members beyond it collapse into the overflow counter. 3 is a specimen choice, not a ruled default.",
      "$status": "PROPOSED #203, Dave's eye owed" },
    { "name": "interactive", "type": "enum", "values": ["none", "members", "group"], "default": "none",
      "$note": "⛔ 'members' is offered at MEDIUM and LARGE ONLY — a 32px interactive disc breaches the ruled 44px min-hit-area. Small sets that must be clickable take 'group': one 44px target for the whole stack.",
      "$status": "PROPOSED #203, Dave's eye owed" },
    { "name": "announce", "type": "enum", "values": ["group", "roster"], "default": "group",
      "$note": "⚠ TWO ACCESSIBLE SHAPES FOR ONE COMPONENT — a decision, not a feature. See $openQuestions.",
      "$status": "PROPOSED #203, Dave's eye owed" }
  ],
  "variants": [
    { "name": "group-announced", "use": "the default — one accessible name for the set, discs hidden from AT; the set is the meaning" },
    { "name": "roster", "use": "a real list where every member is announced; use when the individuals ARE the content" },
    { "name": "members-interactive", "use": "each disc is its own 44px target linking to that person (medium and large only)" },
    { "name": "group-target", "use": "the whole stack is one 44px button — the correct answer for small stacks" }
  ],
  "tokens": {
    "surface": "tertiary/background/hover — the disc fill, from Avatar",
    "ring": "border/subtle — REBOUND, see tokenValidation.rebind",
    "text": "text/default",
    "icon": "icon/default",
    "focus": "focus/ring",
    "page": "background/default",
    "stackRing": "background/default — the 2px separator between overlapping discs. ⚠ see $finding-ring",
    "radius": "50% — EXEMPTION: Avatar is one of the two documented exemptions to the angular brand rule (the other is Badge)"
  },
  "$finding-ring": "⚠ THE ONE REAL WEAKNESS, SHOWN IN THE SPECIMEN RATHER THAN DESCRIBED. The separator ring binds background/default, so the stack only separates correctly ON THE PAGE. Dropped onto a card (tertiary/background/default) or a hover wash, the ring is the wrong colour. In LIGHT mode the card is also white and the defect hides; in DARK mode the page is #1A1A1A and the card is #1F1F1F, so the rings read as dark halos around each disc. The specimen carries an on-card block so Dave can see it in both themes side by side. The honest fixes are a surface-keyed token or a --stack-ring the consumer sets; both are Dave's, and neither is invented here (grey-tint and ink swaps are surface-never-swap items).",
  "relationships": {
    "livesInside": ["List items", "Timeline", "Cards", "Table", "Headers"],
    "commonPatterns": ["approvers on a payment", "members of a shared account", "participants on a thread"],
    "mustNotNeighbour": []
  },
  "accessibility": {
    "relatedSC": ["1.1.1", "1.3.1", "1.4.3", "2.4.7", "2.5.8", "4.1.2"],
    "theCoreDecision": "A stack of discs read out one-by-one is noise ('J L, P A, S O, plus three'). So in the DEFAULT form the GROUP carries the accessible name and the count in words — role=\"img\" with an aria-label naming every visible member AND the overflow ('Approvers: Jordan Lee, Priya Anand, Sam Okafor, and 3 more') — and the individual discs are aria-hidden. This is the PROPOSED reading, not a ruled one.",
    "theAlternative": "The 'roster' variant does the opposite: a real <ul> where each member is announced, the count comes from the list itself, and there is no overflow disc because a roster does not cap. It is for the case where the individuals genuinely are the content.",
    "colourIsNeverAlone": "The overflow counter's '+3' is never the only carrier of the count — the group's accessible name spells it as 'and 3 more'.",
    "targetSize": "Interactive members are built at MEDIUM (44) and LARGE (64) only. The 32px interactive disc is not built at all, because the ruled 44px min-hit-area forbids it and no gate reads that token; enforcement here is by hand, by omission. Small stacks that must be clickable become one 44px group target."
  },
  "antiPatterns": [
    "⛔ Never make a 32px disc interactive — it breaches the ruled 44px min-hit-area, and no gate will catch it for you.",
    "Never announce every disc in the default stacked form; a stack read disc-by-disc is noise, which is the whole reason the group carries the name.",
    "Never let '+3' be the only place the count exists — spell it in the accessible name.",
    "Never use Avatar group where the user must act on individuals one at a time; that is List-items.",
    "Never use the class name 'avatar' for the disc here — canon/type.css binds .avatar to a 14px composite which silently beats the per-size composite on the large disc. The class is avg-face for exactly this reason.",
    "REVIEW Never drop the group onto a card without deciding the separator ring first — the ring binds the page colour and will be wrong (see $finding-ring)."
  ],
  "tokenValidation": {
    "date": "2026-08-19",
    "against": "knowledge/tokens/semantic-colour.json + layout.json, resolved through _validate_snippets.resolve()",
    "result": "PASS — snippet gate rc=0, 0 failures on this file. Every declared var matches the store in BOTH modes. No new token minted; one is PROPOSED (a surface-keyed stack ring) and is Dave's, see $finding-ring.",
    "rebind": "⚠ FINDING, per the gated-component runbook step 2. The gated Avatar's ring var carries a DEPRECATED pair — its light leg exists only in tokens/_manifests/depricate-tokens.json — AND Avatar does not declare that var in its manifest, so _validate_snippets.py has never seen it. This file declares the var and binds it to the live border/subtle (#E1E1E1 light / #808080 dark). Avatar itself was NOT edited: it is a gated shared artefact and the fix is the conductor's to merge.",
    "typeDivergence": "Avatar's large disc uses a raw 24px font-size, which is off the component ramp and part of the type-composite debt. This file uses .t-cm-section-label (20px, weight 500), the nearest ramp rung — a PROPOSED divergence from the parent, declared rather than silent. Small and medium use .t-cm-ctl-12 and .t-cm-ctl-14, which preserve Avatar's weight 500 on-ramp. TYPE-002 contribution: 0."
  },
  "provenance": {
    "source": "gap-report",
    "$note": "Itinerary row 57 (2026-07-14), 'Avatar group — Stacked avatars', P2 Depth. Verified absent first-hand #203 (ls + content grep across avatar/group/stack/cluster/facepile). Built #203 Wave 3b Lane K from the gated Avatar, untouched. No Figma node binds this component."
  },
  "interactive": false,
  "stateModel": "simple",
  "responsive": {
    "behaviour": "inline-flex; the stack does not reflow — it caps. When width is short the answer is a lower max, not a wrap.",
    "$status": "PROPOSED #203, Dave's eye owed"
  },
  "dimensions": {
    "small": 32,
    "medium": 44,
    "large": 64,
    "overlapSmall": -8,
    "overlapMedium": -12,
    "overlapLarge": -16,
    "separatorRing": 2,
    "groupTarget": 44,
    "$note": "Sizes are Avatar's ramp verbatim. Overlap is a quarter of the disc at every size."
  },
  "$openQuestions": [
    "TWO ACCESSIBLE SHAPES FOR ONE COMPONENT is a decision, not a feature. Should Avatar group ship both the group-announced and roster forms, or should one be the component and the other be a documented composition of plain Avatars?",
    "The separator ring's token — see $finding-ring. A surface-keyed token, a consumer-set var, or accept the page-only limitation?",
    "Display cap default of 3 is a specimen choice.",
    "Should the overflow counter be interactive by default (it opens the full set), or passive?",
    "Stacking order: this specimen puts the FIRST member on top, so the set reads left-to-right like a hand of cards. Last-on-top is equally common."
  ]
}

{
  "name": "Combobox",
  "category": "molecule",
  "purpose": "A text input that filters a list of options as the user types, and commits one of them. Use it instead of Dropdown when the option set is long enough that typing beats scrolling — countries, payees, currencies, branches. The value always comes from the list: free text is not accepted.",
  "$provenance-note": "NEW at #203 (wave 3b, lane J) against itinerary row 21 (P2, 'Type-ahead select'). Verified absent first-hand before building: ls knowledge/snippets/ | grep -i combo → nothing; ls knowledge/components/ → no combobox/autocomplete/typeahead meta; grep -rn 'aria-autocomplete' knowledge/snippets/ → 0 hits. The gated Dropdown carries role=\"combobox\" on a BUTTON trigger, which is the select pattern, not this one.",
  "interactive": true,
  "props": [
    { "name": "fieldStyle", "type": "enum", "values": ["boxed", "underline"], "default": "boxed", "$note": "Both gated field styles are supported so a form need not change its field style to gain a combobox. Matches Dropdown, which also keeps both." },
    { "name": "state", "type": "enum", "values": ["default", "hover", "focus", "completed", "disabled", "error"], "default": "default", "$note": "Same state channel as Input-fields/Textarea — inherited, not re-specified." },
    { "name": "open", "type": "boolean", "values": ["false", "true"], "default": "false", "$note": "Behavioural/content-presence state, no token consequence (the s142-D1 class C9 shape)." },
    { "name": "matchEmphasis", "type": "enum", "values": ["underline", "none"], "default": "underline", "$status": "PROPOSED #203, Dave's eye owed — how the matched run is marked. Underline was chosen because weight needs a raw font-weight declaration (TYPE-002 forbids it; there is no .t-cm-* emphasis hook) and colour alone is barred by 1.4.1 and by the red/yellow caution." }
  ],
  "variants": [
    { "name": "boxed", "use": "Full-border field — the default, matching the boxed Input field." },
    { "name": "underline", "use": "Bottom-stroke field — for forms already built on the underline style." }
  ],
  "tokens": {
    "field-background": "form/background/default (transparent), hover form/background/hover",
    "field-border": "form/border/default; focus-within form/border/active + a 4px inset bottom stroke; disabled form/border/disabled; error a 4px inset rag/error stroke (dark: full rag/error border, the Input-fields rule Dave set 2026-07-02)",
    "text": "text/default; disabled text/disabled",
    "icon": "icon/default; disabled icon/disabled",
    "menu-surface": "background/default",
    "menu-elevation": "light elevation/functional (0 0 16px shadow); dark elevation/border (grey outline — shadows are invisible on a near-black page)",
    "menu-divider": "divider/border/section",
    "option-highlight": "form/background/hover fill PLUS a 3px inset rule in form/border/active, so the active row is never colour-alone",
    "focus": "focus/ring",
    "shape": "border-radius/control (field, toggle) and border-radius/surface (floating menu) — the Dropdown split, per-element judgment under ADR-0010",
    "hit-area": "target/min (44px) on the field row, the disclosure toggle and every option row"
  },
  "relationships": {
    "livesInside": ["Form", "Filter bar", "Toolbar", "Dialog"],
    "mustNotNeighbour": [],
    "commonPatterns": ["type-ahead form field", "payee search", "currency picker"]
  },
  "accessibility": {
    "roles": "input[role=combobox] + aria-autocomplete=\"list\" + aria-expanded + aria-controls; the popup is role=listbox with role=option children carrying aria-selected. The highlight is aria-activedescendant, so focus never leaves the input.",
    "keyboard": "Down opens and highlights the first match; Up/Down move the highlight; Enter commits the highlighted option; Escape closes and keeps the typed text; Tab closes and leaves.",
    "announcements": "A polite live region announces the number of matches after each keystroke, and the chosen value on commit. Without it the filtering is invisible to a screen-reader user.",
    "states": "Disabled and error are exposed programmatically (disabled, aria-invalid + aria-describedby). Error is never carried by the red stroke alone — the message pairs a symbol with words and stays ink.",
    "targetArea": "Field row, disclosure toggle and option rows are all 44px (target/min).",
    "relatedSC": ["1.3.1", "1.4.1", "1.4.11", "2.1.1", "2.4.7", "2.5.8", "4.1.2", "4.1.3"]
  },
  "antiPatterns": [
    "Accepting free text. If the user may type a value that is not in the list, that is a different contract (aria-autocomplete=\"both\") or it is Tags-input — do not quietly widen this one.",
    "Marking the matched run with colour or weight alone. Colour fails 1.4.1 and red/yellow are problem hues here; weight would require a raw font declaration TYPE-002 forbids.",
    "Moving DOM focus into the listbox. The input keeps focus; the highlight travels via aria-activedescendant, or the user cannot keep typing.",
    "Filtering silently. Without the polite count announcement a screen-reader user cannot tell the list narrowed.",
    "Using this where the option set is short and browsable — that is the gated Dropdown, and a text field there is friction, not help."
  ],
  "tokenValidation": {
    "date": "2026-08-19",
    "against": "knowledge/tokens/semantic-colour.json via _validate_snippets.py (MONO base only)",
    "result": "PASS — 19 declared vars resolve in both light and dark; 5 declared contrast pairs clear their thresholds in both modes (snippet gate rc=0).",
    "$scope": "The gate reads the MONO base only. The Legacy/Console/Supercharge legs are NOT measured by it. They are shown, not measured, in reviews/REVIEW-203-combobox-four-themes-v1.html — Dave's eye is the instrument there.",
    "$deprecated": "No deprecated tokens are bound. Every binding is a live form/*, text/*, icon/*, rag/*, elevation/*, divider/*, border-radius/* or target/* semantic.",
    "$notGenerated": "knowledge/canon/canon.css carries NO .cn-combobox scope yet — gen_canon_components.py is Lane G's exclusive surface at #203 and no generator was run by this lane. The conductor's regeneration creates it."
  },
  "provenance": {
    "source": "gap-report",
    "figma_node": "",
    "code_path": "",
    "$note": "Itinerary row 21, ITINERARY-2026-07-14-apollo-component-library.xlsx. Mine-from named in the brief: Ant / Untitled. No Figma node exists for this component."
  },
  "edges": {
    "renderedBy": [{ "ref": "snippet:Combobox.reference.html" }],
    "commonPattern": [{ "ref": "pattern:form-field-select" }, { "ref": "pattern:filter-control" }]
  }
}

{
  "name": "Document row",
  "interactive": true,
  "stateModel": "full",
  "$stateModelNote": "REPAIRED #204 (fix sub, post-verifier): this key was authored as \"interactive\", which is not one of meta.schema.json's two enum values ['simple','full'] — the file failed the schema. The authored intent is preserved: the row is interactive (see \"interactive\": true above) and carries hover + focus-visible + active + aria-disabled/pending, i.e. MORE than the 'simple' leg's default+hover/pressed+focus. That is the schema's 'full' state model, which is also the documented default. Mechanical conformance repair only — no semantic was changed and nothing here is a ruling.",
  "category": "molecule",
  "$status": "⚠⚠ PROPOSED #204 (2026-08-19, Lane N) — NOT GATED, NOT PROMOTED, NOT RULED. Built through the gated-component route so it is reviewable at gated fidelity, but every fintech semantic in it is DAVE'S and is marked PROPOSED (the Kpi-tile #203 precedent). Nothing in this file is a ruling. Itinerary row 92, 'Statement / document row · Downloadable document row'.",
  "purpose": "A row in a list of documents the bank has ISSUED to the customer and which they can open or download — statements, certificates, tax documents, contracts. Anatomy: leading file-type glyph + two-line body (document title | optional status, then period/issue date · format · size) + a trailing download control. The defining property is that it carries TWO independent actions per row (open the document; download the file), which is the structural reason it is not a variant of the gated List-items.",
  "props": [
    {
      "name": "actions",
      "type": "enum",
      "values": ["two", "one"],
      "default": "two",
      "$note": "PROPOSED. 'two' = variant A: the row opens/previews the document (stretched link) and a sibling 44×44 button downloads it. 'one' = variant B: the whole row downloads, no preview. ⚠ Variant B IS structurally a List-items row and should be one — it is drawn in the specimen only so Dave can compare the two shapes. If he rules that the product needs only the single-action form, THIS COMPONENT SHOULD NOT EXIST and itinerary row 92 collapses into List-items. That is a live outcome, not a hedge."
    },
    {
      "name": "docType",
      "type": "enum",
      "values": ["statement", "certificate", "tax", "contract", "generic"],
      "default": "statement",
      "$note": "⬛ PROPOSED — P1, DAVE'S. This vocabulary is my wording, chosen to read; no taxonomy has been ratified by anyone. It drives only the leading glyph (document-e-statement / document-pdf / document), all byte-matched from knowledge/assets/icons/, the same library File-upload draws on."
    },
    {
      "name": "status",
      "type": "enum",
      "values": ["none", "new", "action-needed", "expired"],
      "default": "none",
      "$note": "⬛ PROPOSED — P4, DAVE'S. Whether a document row carries a status chip AT ALL is unruled. Shown in the specimen for 'New' (information) and 'Action needed' (warning), because an unread statement and a tax form awaiting signature are genuinely different objects. Equally arguable: documents have no status, only a date. When present the chip is the Status-indicator atom form B, copied VERBATIM from List-items — tint surface + RAG dot + NEUTRAL text label — and every status carries its WORD as well as its hue (1.4.1)."
    },
    {
      "name": "availability",
      "type": "enum",
      "values": ["available", "pending"],
      "default": "available",
      "$note": "'pending' = a statement whose period has not closed. Renders aria-disabled on the row and a native disabled button, and — deliberately — states the REASON in the row's own meta line and in the button's accessible name ('Available from 1 Aug 2026'), so it is never focusable-and-silent."
    },
    {
      "name": "density",
      "type": "enum",
      "values": ["roomy", "compact"],
      "default": "roomy",
      "$note": "⬛ PROPOSED — P6, DAVE'S. --row-h 76 / --row-pad 14 / --label-gap 12 inherited VERBATIM from List-items' roomy default. A statements archive is a long list and may want List-items' 64/10/8 compact leg as ITS default. Not ruled either way."
    }
  ],
  "variants": [
    { "name": "A — two actions", "use": "Default. Row opens/previews the document; trailing 44×44 icon-button downloads it. The form that justifies a separate component." },
    { "name": "B — one action", "use": "Whole row downloads. ⚠ Structurally a List-items row; drawn for comparison only." },
    { "name": "pending", "use": "Document not yet generated; row aria-disabled, reason stated in text." }
  ],
  "$howThisDiffersFromListItems": {
    "$headline": "★ THE CENTRAL ADJUDICATION OF LANE N, RECORDED HERE BECAUSE A READER WILL OTHERWISE REACH FOR THE WRONG COMPONENT.",
    "theStructuralDifference": "In List-items THE WHOLE ROW IS A <button> — `<li><button class=\"row\" type=\"button\">…`, verbatim from List-items.reference.html. That shape supports exactly ONE action per row. A downloadable document row has two actions that are not the same action: (a) open/preview the document, (b) download the file. An interactive control cannot be nested inside a <button>: it is invalid HTML (4.1.1), the inner control is unreachable by keyboard in several ATs, and the outer button's accessible name absorbs the inner one. So the two-action row CANNOT be added as a `type=\"document\"` value on List-items' existing `type` enum without changing List-items' own row ELEMENT for every other variant — and List-items is a gated, promoted, 9.0/9 artefact. This component therefore uses the ROW-WITH-NESTED-ACTION shape: a passive <li> holding a primary <a> whose ::after stretches to the full row, plus a SIBLING <button> raised above it on the z-axis. Two independent targets, both ≥44px, no nesting.",
    "whatWasCopiedNotRedrawn": "The row shell (ul/li borders, surface, divider), the two-line body geometry (title|status / meta), the density tokens (--row-h / --row-pad / --label-gap), the hover trick where the leading disc flips to the default surface so it separates from the hover tint, and the Status-indicator form-B chip — ALL copied from List-items.reference.html. The 44×44 hit area and 18px glyph come from Icon-button. The file-type glyphs are byte-matched from knowledge/assets/icons/media/, the same library File-upload uses. List-items was NOT edited.",
    "whatWasDeliberatelyNotCopied": "List-items' raw font declarations (`font:500 16px/1.35 var(--font)` etc). Its ANATOMY was copied; its type debt was not. This file declares no raw font in component scope and contributes 0 to the shrink-only ratchet.",
    "theRoundToSquareChange": "List-items' leading visual is the round Avatar disc — the documented round exemption, which exists for PEOPLE. A file is not a person, so the leading slot here is the same 36px size but SQUARE (border-radius/indicator), which console forks to 4px through the cascade exactly as it does for List-items' own indicator atoms. No exemption is claimed.",
    "whenToChooseWhich": "Choose List-items (transaction) when the row is a MONEY EVENT the reader may open — a payment, a transfer, a card purchase. Choose Document row when the row is a FILE the reader may open or take away. The tell: a document row has no amount and a transaction row has no file."
  },
  "$howThisDiffersFromFileUpload": {
    "direction": "File-upload (GATED, itinerary row 18) is the INBOUND direction: files the user is giving the bank, mid-transfer, with a progress bar, a size-validation error state and a REMOVE (×) control. Its rows are ephemeral — they exist only during the interaction. Document row is the OUTBOUND direction: files the bank has already issued, complete, persistent, with a DOWNLOAD control, no progress and no removal.",

    "Carrying status by the RAG dot alone. The label is the carrier; the warning dot is under 3:1 standalone.",
    "Shipping a pending/unavailable row with no stated reason — an aria-disabled row that says nothing is a dead end for every reader, not just AT users."

    "P1 — DOCUMENT-TYPE VOCABULARY (statement / certificate / tax / contract / generic). My wording, unratified. Store search that failed to settle it: direct grep of knowledge/_rulings.json (203 entries) for `transaction|ledger|statement row|document row|line[- ]item|debit|credit` → 16 entries matched the word 'ledger' and ALL 16 use it in the record-keeping sense (a decisions ledger, a token-fork ledger, an exceptions ledger); ZERO concern a document or statement COMPONENT. Alternatives: a text link ('Download PDF'), whole-row download (variant B), or an overflow menu when several formats exist. ⚠ s182-D2 is cited in the specimen as PRECEDENT for a label-less trailing affordance; it governs the trend card and NOT this component, so it is precedent, not authority.",

{
  "name": "Footer",
  "category": "organism",
  "$status": "PROPOSED #204, Dave's eye owed. Nothing in this file is a ruling. Built in Lane M of the s203-D2 PM-topology trial from itinerary row 81 ('Footer — Incl. doormat / mega-footer', Layout & containers, P2), verified genuinely absent first-hand.",
  "purpose": "The SITE FOOTER: the contentinfo landmark at the end of a page, carrying the link groups a reader goes looking for, the legal links a regulator requires, and the copyright line. Two forms — a doormat (mega-footer) for pages a reader browses, and a slim legal bar for authenticated application screens where a four-column mat would be in the way.",
  "$vocabularyCollision": "★★ DECLARED BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE, because this is the s202-D3 class — the class where Dave rejected a build because one word carried two meanings and every assertion stayed green. In this repo 'footer' ALREADY means the LAYOUT FOOTER of a container: Drawer's footer actions, Modals' dialog footer, Data-grid's pagination footer, Command-palette's hint bar. The gated ACTION-BAR describes itself, verbatim, as 'A footer bar that pins a screen/flow's actions'. This component is the OTHER footer — the document's end matter. The two can appear on the same screen (an Action-bar pinned above a site Footer) and they are not variants of one another. ⛔ IF THIS COMPONENT KEEPS THE NAME 'Footer' IT INHERITS THE COLLISION. Renaming is Dave's; nothing here renames anything.",
  "$differsFromNeighbours": {
    "Links": "Links owns the link ATOM and already ships .related, which its own source calls 'the footer / utility pattern' — a wrapping list of related links. Footer is the REGION that arranges them: the landmark, the named columns, the legal bar, the copyright, the rule that separates the page from its end matter. THE TELL: strip the landmark and the group headings from a Footer and what is left is a .related list, and it should be one. links.meta.json already declares context:footer with a Footer relationship — the component graph anticipated this component before it existed.",
    "Action-bar": "See $vocabularyCollision. Action-bar pins the ACTIONS of a flow and belongs to the task; its contents change per screen. Footer is the end of the DOCUMENT and belongs to the site; its contents do not change per screen.",
    "Headers": "The masthead sibling. A header carries wayfinding a reader is about to use; a footer carries the links they went looking for and the text the regulator requires. A doormat that simply duplicates the masthead is a doormat that has stopped being read.",
    "Navigations / Sidebar-nav": "Those model STATE — current page, expansion, sections, disclosure. A doormat is flat and stateless; the only state it carries is aria-current=\"page\", inherited from the Links atom unchanged."
  },
  "props": [
    {
      "name": "form",
      "type": "enum",
      "values": [
        "doormat",
        "slim"
      ],
      "default": "doormat",
      "$note": "doormat = brand statement + back-to-top + named link columns + legal bar. slim = legal bar and copyright only. Which surfaces get which is a product decision and is NOT settled here.",
      "$status": "PROPOSED #204, Dave's eye owed"
    },
    {
      "name": "groups",
      "type": "array",
      "default": [],
      "$note": "Each group is a <nav> with aria-labelledby pointing at its own heading, so a screen-reader user gets four named navigation landmarks rather than one anonymous list of forty links. The specimen shows four groups; the auto-fit track floor is 180px.",
      "$status": "PROPOSED #204, Dave's eye owed"
    },
    {
      "name": "backToTop",
      "type": "boolean",
      "default": true,
      "$note": "The arrow link from the gated Links atom, rotated to point up, glyph byte-matched from arrows-and-chevrons/arrow-up.svg. 44px tall.",
      "$status": "PROPOSED #204, Dave's eye owed"
    }
  ],
  "variants": [
    {
      "name": "doormat",
      "use": "the end of a marketing or servicing page — the reader may still be looking for something"
    },
    {
      "name": "slim",
      "use": "the end of an authenticated application screen — the reader came to do one thing and is finishing it"
    }
  ],
  "slots": {
    "brand": {
      "accepts": {
        "capability": [
          "statement"
        ]
      },
      "required": false,
      "use": "the short statement or brand line that opens a mega-footer, beside the back-to-top link",
      "$status": "PROPOSED #204, Dave's eye owed"
    }
  },
  "tokens": {
    "page": "background/default",
    "surface": "surface/subtle — the footer band, so the end matter reads as a band rather than as more page",
    "divider": "divider/border/section — the 1px rule between the page and the footer",
    "subdivider": "divider/border/subsection — inside the footer, between the brand block, the mat and the legal bar",
    "text": "text/default",
    "muted": "text/secondary",
    "icon": "icon/default",
    "focus": "focus/ring",
    "radius": "border-radius/control — the link focus shape only; there is no other radius in this component",
    "target": "target/min (44px)",
    "$rag": "NONE. No RAG value appears anywhere in this component — there is no status here to carry."
  },
  "$finding-44px-cost": "⚠ EVERY footer link is a >= 44px target at EVERY width, not only when stacked. That is STRICTER than the gated Links .related pattern, which grows its targets only at <=420px, and it is a visible design cost: a four-column doormat with four links per column becomes measurably taller than the compact typographic ideal a footer usually aims for. The trade is a design decision, not a technicality — see $decisionsForDave 2. No gate reads the target token for hit area, so this was MEASURED in a real browser rather than assumed.",
  "$finding-type-debt-conflict": "★★ 'COPY THE APPROVED ARTEFACT VERBATIM' AND 'ADD ZERO TO THE SHRINK-ONLY TYPE RATCHET' CONFLICT WHEN THE APPROVED ARTEFACT IS ITSELF IN DEBT. The gated Links atom writes font-weight:500 twice in its own CSS — on a.arrow and on a.lnk[aria-current=\"page\"] — and those are exactly the raw declarations TYPE-002 counts. Copying them verbatim DROVE _validate_type_composites.py red on this file (measured #204: 2 violations). The emphasis therefore arrives here through canon/type.css's own .t-ed-body-small .em modifier, applied in the MARKUP (the T-D14 markup-class route): identical rendered weight, zero added debt. Links itself was NOT edited — it is a gated shared artefact and its two declarations are the BUILD-PM's to retire. THE DIVERGENCE FROM THE PARENT IS DECLARED, NOT HIDDEN.",
  "relationships": {
    "livesInside": [
      "Template — page",
      "Template — authenticated app shell"
    ],
    "commonPatterns": [
      "site end matter",
      "legal bar",
      "utility navigation"
    ],
    "mustNotNeighbour": []
  },
  "accessibility": {
    "relatedSC": [
      "1.3.1",
      "1.4.1",
      "1.4.3",
      "1.4.10",
      "2.4.1",
      "2.4.4",
      "2.4.7",
      "2.4.8",
      "2.5.8"
    ],
    "landmark": "<footer role=\"contentinfo\"> with an aria-label naming which footer it is ('Site footer' / 'Legal footer'), so a page carrying both a doormat and a slim bar does not present two anonymous contentinfo landmarks.",
    "grouping": "Each link column is a <nav> with aria-labelledby pointing at its own visible heading. Forty links in one anonymous list is not navigable; four named landmarks are.",
    "currentPage": "aria-current=\"page\" marked by WEIGHT plus a persistent 2px underline — never colour alone. Inherited from the Links atom; the weight arrives by composite modifier rather than by raw declaration (see $finding-type-debt-conflict).",
    "linkText": "Every link names its destination. No 'click here', no 'more', no 'read more' — the aca-004 class the snippet gate blocks.",
    "targetSize": "Every link is a >= 44px target at every width. MEASURED, not assumed; no gate reads the target token for hit area.",
    "colourIsNeverAlone": "Links are distinguished by an underline, not by colour. No RAG value appears in this component at all."
  },
  "antiPatterns": [
    "Never let a doormat duplicate the masthead navigation. A footer that repeats the header is a footer that has stopped being read.",
    "Never put the primary task's actions in a site Footer. That is an Action-bar, and the two are different components that share a word.",
    "Never ship an anonymous <footer> with no aria-label on a page that also has a container footer — a screen-reader user then has two contentinfo regions and no way to tell them apart.",
    "Never let a link column exceed what a reader will scan. If a group needs more than about six links it is two groups, or it is a page.",
    "Never carry legal text as an image or a PDF-only link with no text alternative in the bar itself.",
    "REVIEW Never promote, gate or register this component without Dave's word. It is PROPOSED #204, and the name, the 44px trade and the band colour are all open."
  ],
  "tokenValidation": {
    "date": "2026-08-19",
    "against": "knowledge/tokens/semantic-colour.json + layout.json, resolved through _validate_snippets.resolve()",
    "result": "PASS — snippet gate rc=0, 0 failures repo-wide with this file present. Every declared var matches the store in BOTH modes. a11y gate rc=0. Type-composite gate rc=0 on this file after the .em rebind; repo-wide 1097, unchanged — this file adds 0 to the shrink-only ratchet.",
    "declaredAbsence": "No RAG pair is declared because no RAG value is painted. The declared pairs are the four neutral ones: text/default and text/secondary on surface/subtle, icon/default on surface/subtle (held to 4.5 by icon-015), and text/default on background/default.",
    "notRun": "_validate_state_contrast.py was NOT run: a filtered run overwrites the tracked _STATE-CONTRAST-AUDIT.md and Lane M held no shared-file licence. Declared and owed to the BUILD-PM.",
    "notRegistered": "Absent from knowledge/component-types.json (a shared file, outside the lane fence).",
    "renderProof": "See the receipt at notes/_receipts/2026-08-19-204-wave-laneM-feedback-layout.md for the driven figures."
  },
  "provenance": {
    "source": "gap-report",
    "$note": "Itinerary row 81 (2026-07-14 sheet): 'Footer — Incl. doormat / mega-footer', Layout & containers, P2. Confirmed a TRUE gap at #204 by filename greps under every plausible alias, a content grep over knowledge/snippets and knowledge/components (whose five 'footer' hits are all the OTHER footer — Drawer, Modals, Data-grid, Command-palette, Action-bar), and a direct grep of knowledge/_rulings.json (the store itself, not the retrieval index, which _capture_gate.py --selftest reports STALE). Built #204 Lane M from one gated parent (Links), untouched. No Figma node binds this component; provenance.figma_node stays empty until a design owner binds it."
  },
  "interactive": true,
  "stateModel": "simple",
  "responsive": {
    "mat": "auto-fit grid, minmax(180px, 1fr), collapsing to one column below a 560px CONTAINER width — a container query, so a footer inside a narrow panel collapses on a wide screen",
    "legal": "the legal list stacks below the same container width; the copyright line moves beneath it",
    "targets": "nothing has to grow at narrow widths because everything is already 44px at every width — that is the point of deciding it once",
    "$status": "PROPOSED #204, Dave's eye owed"
  },
  "dimensions": {
    "innerMaxWidth": 1120,
    "innerPaddingX": 16,
    "innerPaddingY": 32,
    "matMinTrack": 180,
    "matGap": [
      24,
      16
    ],
    "linkMinHeight": 44,
    "$note": "innerPaddingX 16 is layout/app/margin. linkMinHeight 44 is target/min. innerMaxWidth 1120, matMinTrack 180 and the 32px vertical padding are specimen choices, not ruled."
  },
  "$decisionsForDave": [
    "1 · THE NAME. 'Footer' already means a container's action row in this repo, and the gated Action-bar uses the word about itself. Site-footer? End-matter? Doormat? Renaming is yours, and this file deliberately does not do it.",
    "2 · THE 44px TRADE. Every footer link here is a 44px target at every width, which makes a doormat noticeably taller than the compact ideal. Accept the height, or grow targets only when stacked as the gated Links .related pattern does?",
    "3 · THE BAND COLOUR. The footer sits on surface/subtle so it reads as a band. In Mono light that is #F0F0F0 against a #FFFFFF page — a quiet distinction. Should it be a band at all, or should the section rule carry the whole separation?",
    "4 · TWO FORMS OR TWO COMPONENTS? The doormat and the slim bar share a landmark, a legal row and a link atom, and share nothing else. One component with a form prop, or two components?",
    "5 · WHAT BELONGS IN THE LEGAL BAR. Privacy, terms, cookies and accessibility are the specimen's four. That list is regulatory, it varies by market, and it is not mine to fix.",
    "6 · BACK-TO-TOP. Present by default here. On a short page it is noise; on a long one it is the most-used link in the footer. Default on, default off, or a consumer decision?"
  ],
  "$copiedFrom": [
    "Links (the a.lnk inline link atom and the a.arrow CTA link, both verbatim)",
    "Sidebar-nav / Drawer (the 1px section-divider recipe)"
  ],
  "$relationshipsNote": "May legitimately appear on the same screen as an Action-bar. They are not variants; see $vocabularyCollision."
}

{
  "name": "Grid / stack utilities",
  "category": "atom",
  "$status": "PROPOSED #204, Dave's eye owed. Nothing in this file is a ruling. Built in Lane M of the s203-D2 PM-topology trial from itinerary row 82 ('Grid / stack utilities — Layout primitives', Layout & containers, P2), verified genuinely absent first-hand.",
  "purpose": "Seven content-agnostic layout primitives — container, stack, row, grid, twelve-column, split and measure — that arrange arbitrary blocks in space and then get out of the way. They paint nothing, size no type, and announce nothing. The class prefix is .l-.",
  "$notTheDataGrid": "⛔⛔ THIS IS NOT ROW 51's DATA-GRID, AND THE ITINERARY'S OWN WARNING ABOUT THAT IS CORRECT. The gated Data-grid is a DATA TABLE: rows that are records, columns that are fields, role=\"grid\", sorting, selection, pagination, a footer read-out. Everything here is SPACE. A layout grid has no data, no roles, no semantics and nothing to announce. THE TELL: a Data-grid's columns MEAN something (they are fields); a layout grid's columns mean NOTHING (they are gaps between things). This is the SECOND vocabulary collision Lane M found — see footer.meta.json for the first — and it is the s202-D3 class, where Dave rejected a build because one word carried two meanings and every assertion stayed green. The slug is layout-utilities and the prefix is .l- precisely so this does not claim the word 'grid' at the component level. NAMING IS DAVE'S.",
  "$measuredGap": "★★ WHAT THE GAP ACTUALLY IS, MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSERTED. The recipe this component would own is already hand-written in THIRTEEN gated snippets, and they do not agree with each other. Probed #204: grep -rn \"repeat(auto-\\(fill\\|fit\\), *minmax\" knowledge/snippets/ → 13 files. minmax FLOOR: 180px (Footer, this lane) · 240px (Stat-card, Kpi-tile) · 300px (Time-picker, Form-layout, File-upload, Secure-entry, Textarea, Date-range-picker, Amount-input, Input-fields, Date-picker, Cards). GAP: 16px · 20px (Cards ×2) · '24px 32px' (the nine form-family snippets) · '24px 16px'. MAX-WIDTH: 760px (form family) · 800px (Stat-card, Kpi-tile) · none (Cards). KEYWORD: auto-fill in eleven, auto-fit in Cards twice — and that is a REAL behavioural difference, not a stylistic one: auto-fit collapses empty tracks and stretches the survivors, auto-fill keeps them. Two snippets behave differently from the other eleven and nothing in the repo records that as a decision. ⛔ THIS COMPONENT RECONCILES NONE OF THEM. Picking one floor, one gap and one keyword for the whole system is a ruling, and rulings are Dave's. The thirteen existing snippets were not touched.",
  "$storeReachLimits": "⛔⛔ TWO THINGS THE TOKEN STORE CANNOT REACH FROM A SNIPPET, BOTH DECLARED, NEITHER GLOSSED. (1) THE SPACING SCALE IS UNREACHABLE BY THE SNIPPET GATE. tokens/spacing.json holds the whole gap ramp — gap/fixed/content/{xxsmall 2, xsmall 4, small 8, medium 12}, gap/fixed/subsection/{xsmall 24, small 32, medium 40, large 48}, gap/fixed/section/{xsmall 48 … xlarge 120}, padding/fixed/{small 12, medium 16, large 20, xlarge 24} — but _validate_snippets.resolve() loads semantic-colour, layout, motion, opacity and component-types ONLY. spacing.json is not in its namespace list, so declaring --l-gap-s: gap/fixed/content/small in the manifest fails with \"token not found in store\". THE ONE COMPONENT WHOSE ENTIRE SUBJECT IS SPACING IS THE ONE COMPONENT THAT CANNOT BIND ITS OWN VALUES THROUGH THE GATE. The steps are therefore literal values, each carrying its token path in a comment, and the manifest declares only what the gate can actually check. A gate fix is proposed to the BUILD-PM; nothing was patched here. (2) A BREAKPOINT TOKEN CAN NEVER BE BOUND IN CSS AT ALL — @media and @container conditions cannot consume custom properties. That is a CSS language fact, not a repo defect. breakpoint/s (480px), breakpoint/ms (760px) and breakpoint/m (960px) are written literally in the query conditions with their token paths in comments, and are deliberately NOT declared in the manifest: declaring a var the component does not consume would be a green assertion about nothing.",
  "$primitiveDeliberatelyNotBuilt": "⛔ The classic name for the 'two items side by side until they run out of room, then stacked' primitive is a SWITCHER. In this repo 'switch' is RULED vocabulary — s202-D3, where it means THE THUMB of a toggle. Naming a layout utility 'switcher' would manufacture exactly the collision this component opens by warning about. The behaviour is covered by .l-grid with a high floor; if a dedicated primitive is wanted it needs a name that is not 'switch', and that name is Dave's. DECLARED, not silently omitted.",
  "$differsFromNeighbours": {
    "Data-grid": "See $notTheDataGrid. Data, not space.",
    "Cards": "Cards owns the SURFACE — the box, its border, its padding, its content order — and hand-rolls a .row grid to sit several of them side by side. These utilities own the ARRANGEMENT and nothing else. THE TELL: a Card without a grid is still a Card; a grid without anything in it is nothing at all.",
    "Form-layout": "The form-specific organism: label/field/help relationships, fieldset grouping, error placement. It hand-rolls the same 300px / '24px 32px' grid that nine of its siblings do. Form-layout is layout WITH SEMANTICS; this is layout with none.",
    "Eyebrow": "Checked for overlap because the lane brief named it; there is none. Eyebrow is a kicker label above a heading, a <span>, with no layout role."
  },

The count is written as repeat(12, …) with the token path in a comment. Declared, not hidden.",

    "$demoChrome": "page background/default · surface tertiary/background/default · fill surface/subtle · border border/subtle · text text/default · focus focus/ring. ALL DEMO CHROME: the primitives themselves paint nothing.",

    "relatedSC": [
      "1.3.2",
      "1.4.10",

    "semantics": "NONE, deliberately. A layout primitive announces nothing and carries no role. Anything that needs a role — a list, a table, a navigation — is a different component and should be one. Putting role=\"grid\" on .l-cols would lie to assistive technology about what the columns mean.",
    "readingOrder": "The primitives never reorder content visually away from the DOM order (1.3.2). No order, row-reverse, column-reverse or grid-area placement appears anywhere in this file, and that is a constraint on the primitives rather than an accident of the specimen.",
    "reflow": "Verified at 1400px and 480px. .l-grid's min(var(--l-min), 100%) wrapper is what stops a 300px floor from forcing a horizontal scroll at 320px — the failure several of the hand-rolled copies can still produce.",

  },
  "antiPatterns": [
    "Never put a role on a layout primitive. If it needs a role it is not a layout primitive.",
    "Never use .l-cols for tabular data. That is Data-grid or Table, and the columns there mean something.",
    "Never let a child add its own vertical margin inside .l-stack. The stack owns the rhythm; two owners produce a rhythm neither of them chose.",
    "Never set a .l-grid floor wider than the narrowest container it will live in without the min() wrapper — that is how a 300px floor produces a horizontal scrollbar at 320px.",
    "Never reach for a viewport media query when the thing that ran out of room is the CONTAINER. .l-split shows the case: the same markup collapses inside a 420px frame on a 1400px screen.",
    "Never name a layout primitive 'switcher'. 'switch' is ruled vocabulary in this system and means the thumb of a toggle (s202-D3).",
    "REVIEW Never promote, gate or register this component without Dave's word. It is PROPOSED #204, and the name, the ramp, the default floor and the auto-fill/auto-fit default are all open."
  ],
  "tokenValidation": {
    "date": "2026-08-19",
    "against": "knowledge/tokens/semantic-colour.json + layout.json, resolved through _validate_snippets.resolve()",
    "result": "PASS — snippet gate rc=0, 0 failures repo-wide with this file present. Every declared var matches the store in BOTH modes. a11y gate rc=0. Type-composite gate rc=0 on this file; repo-wide 1097, unchanged — this file adds 0 to the shrink-only ratchet.",
    "declaredAbsence": "The spacing ramp and the breakpoints are NOT declared in the manifest, and both absences are deliberate and explained in $storeReachLimits: the first because the gate's resolver cannot reach spacing.json, the second because CSS query conditions cannot consume custom properties at all. Declaring either would be a green assertion about nothing.",
    "notRun": "_validate_state_contrast.py was NOT run: a filtered run overwrites the tracked _STATE-CONTRAST-AUDIT.md and Lane M held no shared-file licence. Declared and owed to the BUILD-PM.",
    "notRegistered": "Absent from knowledge/component-types.json (a shared file, outside the lane fence).",
    "renderProof": "See the receipt at notes/_receipts/2026-08-19-204-wave-laneM-feedback-layout.md for the driven figures."
  },
  "provenance": {
    "source": "gap-report",
    "$note": "Itinerary row 82 (2026-07-14 sheet): 'Grid / stack utilities — Layout primitives', Layout & containers, P2, with the sheet's own explicit warning that this is NOT row 51's Data-grid. Confirmed a TRUE gap at #204 by filename greps under every plausible alias (grid, stack, layout, util, container, column, flex, spacing), a content grep over knowledge/snippets and knowledge/components (zero hits for grid utilit / stack utilit / layout-utilities / layout util / flexbox / spacing scale), and a direct grep of knowledge/_rulings.json (the store itself, not the retrieval index, which _capture_gate.py --selftest reports STALE). Built #204 Lane M. No Figma node binds this component; provenance.figma_node stays empty until a design owner binds it."
  },
  "interactive": false,
  "stateModel": "simple",
  "responsive": {
    "l-grid": "intrinsic — no query at all; the track floor plus min(…, 100%) does the work",
    "l-cols": "spans collapse to full width below breakpoint/ms (760px), a VIEWPORT query, because an explicit column grid is a page-level frame and a page-level frame answers to the page",
    "l-split": "collapses below a 760px CONTAINER width, a container query, because a split inside a narrow panel should collapse on a wide screen and a viewport query cannot see that",
    "$status": "PROPOSED #204, Dave's eye owed"
  },
  "dimensions": {
    "containerMaxWidth": 1120,
    "containerInset": 16,
    "columns": 12,
    "columnGap": 16,
    "gridFloorDefault": 240,
    "splitRail": 280,
    "measure": "64ch",
    "gapRamp": [
      2,
      4,
      8,
      12,
      24,
      32,
      48
    ],
    "$note": "containerInset 16 is layout/app/margin, columnGap 16 is layout/app/gutter, columns 12 is layout/web/columns. gridFloorDefault 240 is Stat-card's and Kpi-tile's value, copied. containerMaxWidth 1120, splitRail 280 and measure 64ch are specimen choices and are not ruled. The gapRamp values are tokens/spacing.json's, written literally because the gate cannot resolve them."
  },
  "$decisionsForDave": [
    "1 · THE NAME. 'Grid' already means the Data-grid in this repo. The slug here is layout-utilities and the prefix .l-, which avoids claiming the word — but that is an avoidance, not a decision. What should this be called?",
    "2 · ONE FLOOR, ONE GAP, ONE KEYWORD. Thirteen gated snippets disagree today: floors of 180/240/300, gaps of 16 / 20 / '24 32' / '24 16', and auto-fill in eleven versus auto-fit in Cards twice. Ruling a single set is what turns this from a specimen into a primitive — and it is a ruling, so it is yours.",
    "3 · SHOULD THE THIRTEEN MIGRATE? If they do, thirteen gated snippets change and every one needs re-gating. If they do not, this primitive is documentation rather than machinery.",
    "4 · THE GAP RAMP'S SHAPE. Seven steps drawn from two token ramps that MEET at 48px (gap/fixed/subsection/large and gap/fixed/section/xsmall are the same number). Seven named steps, or fewer?",
    "5 · CONTAINER QUERIES OR VIEWPORT QUERIES, AS A RULE. This file uses one for .l-split and the other for .l-cols and explains why each time. A system-level rule would remove the explaining.",
    "6 · THE MISSING 'SWITCHER'. Deliberately not built because the obvious name collides with ruled vocabulary. Is the behaviour wanted, and if so under what name?",
    "7 · IS 64ch THE MEASURE? It appears by hand in several snippets already. One number, ruled once, or a consumer choice?"
  ],
  "$copiedFrom": [
    "Stat-card / Kpi-tile (the auto-fill minmax grid recipe, copied then parameterised)",
    "Cards (the demo block surface recipe)"
  ],
  "$wouldAbsorb": "Thirteen gated snippets currently hand-roll .l-grid's recipe: Time-picker, Form-layout, File-upload, Stat-card, Secure-entry, Textarea, Date-range-picker, Cards (×2), Amount-input, Input-fields, Date-picker, Kpi-tile, Footer. ⛔ NONE of them was touched. Migrating them is a ruling plus a wave, not a lane's chore.",
  "$categoryNote": "⚠ CATEGORY IS 'atom' BY SCHEMA CONSTRAINT, NOT BY CONVICTION. meta.schema.json's category enum is the atomic-design ladder — atom / molecule / organism / template / page — and it has no rung for a LAYOUT PRIMITIVE, which is not a thing on the page at all but the space between things. 'primitive' was written first and DROVE the schema red, verbatim: \"'primitive' is not one of ['atom','molecule','organism','template','page']\". meta.schema.json is a shared file outside Lane M's fence and was NOT edited; 'atom' is the nearest legal rung and the divergence is declared here rather than hidden. Whether the ladder should grow a primitive rung is a decision, and it is Dave's.",
  "$stateModelNote": "'simple' by schema enum (only 'simple' and 'full' are legal). The real model is NONE: a layout primitive has no default, hover, focus or pressed state because there is nothing to press. The enum has no rung for a stateless primitive — the same shape as $categoryNote."
}

{
  "name": "Multi-select",
  "category": "molecule",
  "purpose": "Choose several values from a fixed list and keep them visible. The field holds a filtering input; the list stays open while choices are made; each choice appears as a removable chip. Use it for statement accounts, filter facets, recipients — anywhere the answer is a set rather than a value.",
  "$provenance-note": "NEW at #203 (wave 3b, lane J) against itinerary row 22 (P2, 'Chips-in-field selection'). Verified absent first-hand: ls knowledge/snippets/ | grep -i multi → only Chart-combo/other unrelated names; no multi-select meta; grep -rn 'aria-multiselectable' knowledge/snippets/ → 0 hits. The gated Dropdown META lists a 'multi-select (non-native)' VARIANT, but its snippet implements single-select only (its own header says 'CANONICAL REFERENCE for the non-native single-select Dropdown'), so the variant was documented and never built.",
  "interactive": true,
  "props": [
    { "name": "display", "type": "enum", "values": ["chips-in-field", "count-summary"], "default": "chips-in-field", "$status": "PROPOSED #203, Dave's eye owed. Both are built. Chips-in-field keeps every choice visible but grows the field; count-summary keeps the field one row tall and moves the chips beneath it. Which is the default is a design decision, not this lane's to rule." },
    { "name": "state", "type": "enum", "values": ["default", "hover", "focus", "disabled", "error"], "default": "default", "$note": "Same state channel as Input-fields/Textarea — inherited, not re-specified." },
    { "name": "open", "type": "boolean", "values": ["false", "true"], "default": "false", "$note": "Behavioural/content-presence state, no token consequence." },
    { "name": "max", "type": "number", "$note": "Optional ceiling on the number of selections. Not exercised in the reference — the limit story is demonstrated on Tags-input, where free entry makes it load-bearing." }
  ],
  "variants": [
    { "name": "chips-in-field", "use": "Every selection visible and individually removable; the field wraps and grows." },
    { "name": "count-summary", "use": "The field states the count and stays one row tall, so dense forms and toolbars do not reflow as choices are made." }
  ],
  "tokens": {
    "field-background": "form/background/default (transparent), hover form/background/hover",
    "field-border": "form/border/default; focus-within form/border/active + a 4px inset bottom stroke; disabled form/border/disabled; error a 4px inset rag/error stroke (dark: full rag/error border)",
    "chip": "INHERITED FROM TAGS — 1px form/border/default on a transparent fill, border-radius/control (square in Mono), label text/default, dismiss glyph icon/default. No new chip tokens are introduced.",
    "text": "text/default; disabled text/disabled",
    "icon": "icon/default; disabled icon/disabled",
    "menu-surface": "background/default",
    "menu-elevation": "light elevation/functional; dark elevation/border (grey outline)",
    "menu-divider": "divider/border/section",
    "option-highlight": "form/background/hover fill PLUS a 3px inset rule in form/border/active — never colour-alone",
    "focus": "focus/ring",
    "shape": "border-radius/control (field, chip, toggle), border-radius/surface (floating menu)",
    "hit-area": "target/min (44px) on the field row, the disclosure toggle and every option row. The chip dismiss button is 24px — the gated Tags value, inherited unchanged."
  },
  "relationships": {
    "livesInside": ["Form", "Filter bar", "Toolbar", "Dialog"],
    "mustNotNeighbour": [],
    "commonPatterns": ["multi-select facet list", "statement account picker", "recipient picker"]
  },
  "accessibility": {
    "roles": "input[role=combobox] + aria-autocomplete=\"list\" + aria-expanded + aria-controls; popup role=listbox with aria-multiselectable=\"true\" and role=option children carrying aria-selected. Highlight via aria-activedescendant — focus never leaves the input.",
    "keyboard": "Down opens; Up/Down move the highlight; Enter toggles the highlighted option WITHOUT closing; Escape closes; Backspace on an empty input removes the last selection. Each chip's dismiss button is in the tab order.",
    "announcements": "A polite live region announces the selection count after every change, because the visual chip appears outside the reading order of the user's current position.",
    "states": "Disabled and error exposed programmatically (disabled, aria-invalid + aria-describedby). The error message pairs a symbol with words and stays ink.",
    "targetArea": "Field row, toggle and option rows 44px. Chip dismiss 24px (WCAG 2.5.8 minimum) — inherited from Tags, flagged rather than silently raised.",
    "relatedSC": ["1.3.1", "1.4.1", "1.4.11", "2.1.1", "2.4.7", "2.5.8", "4.1.2", "4.1.3"]
  },
  "antiPatterns": [
    "Closing the list after each choice. The whole point is picking several without re-opening.",
    "Drawing a second chip. The chip is the gated Tags chip; if it changes, it changes in Tags first.",
    "Confusing this chip with the Selection-controls chip. That one is a toggle the user presses directly; this one is a receipt of a choice made in the list, and removal is its only interaction.",
    "Leaving the selection count unannounced — a chip added below the caret is invisible to a screen-reader user.",
    "Silently truncating the chip row. If the field must stay one row tall, use the count-summary variant, which says how many are chosen, rather than hiding choices."
  ],
  "tokenValidation": {
    "date": "2026-08-19",
    "against": "knowledge/tokens/semantic-colour.json via _validate_snippets.py (MONO base only)",
    "result": "PASS — 19 declared vars resolve in both light and dark; 5 declared contrast pairs clear their thresholds in both modes (snippet gate rc=0).",
    "$scope": "MONO base only. The other three themes are shown, not measured, in reviews/REVIEW-203-multi-select-four-themes-v1.html.",
    "$deprecated": "No deprecated tokens bound. Note that the gated Tags META still records deprecated fills for the FILLED chip; this component uses the OUTLINED chip the Tags SNIPPET actually ships, which is already rebound onto form/*.",
    "$notGenerated": "canon.css carries NO .cn-multi-select scope yet — no generator was run by this lane (Lane G owns that surface at #203)."
  },
  "provenance": {
    "source": "gap-report",

    "$note": "Itinerary row 22. Mine-from named in the brief: Ant / Carbon. No Figma node; the Dropdown node's multi-select variant was documented in dropdown.meta.json but never implemented."

{
  "name": "Payment card visual",
  "category": "molecule",
  "purpose": "A passive representation of a PHYSICAL PAYMENT INSTRUMENT — the card face, at ID-1 proportions, showing which piece of plastic this is and whether it is usable right now. Product name, masked number, cardholder, expiry, a contactless indicator, and a status chip carrying a word. It carries NO balance, deliberately. PROPOSED #204 (itinerary row 93, slug payment-card-visual) — NOT GATED, NOT RULED. Fintech semantics are Dave's (the Kpi-tile precedent, s182-D2).",
  "intent": "identity",
  "props": [
    { "name": "productName", "type": "string", "$note": "Rendered in the Tags atom (square outline), copied from Tags.reference via Account-card. E.g. 'Business debit'." },
