records.head: Popconfirm · molecule · An anchored confirm-in-place: a small bubble that opens beside the object being acted on,  · edges=0
records.text:
{
  "name": "Popconfirm",
  "category": "molecule",
  "$status": "PROPOSED #204, Dave's eye owed. Nothing in this file is a ruling. Built in Lane M of the s203-D2 PM-topology trial from itinerary row 75 ('Popconfirm — Inline confirm-in-place', Feedback & status, P2), verified genuinely absent first-hand before a line was written.",
  "purpose": "An anchored confirm-in-place: a small bubble that opens beside the object being acted on, asks one question, and offers exactly two exits — cancel and confirm. Use it when a single action needs a check but not an interruption, and the reader benefits from still seeing the thing they are about to change. A Popover ANSWERS; a Popconfirm ASKS.",
  "$differsFromNeighbours": {
    "Popover": "The closest neighbour, and the one whose bubble chrome this copies verbatim (surface, elevation border, functional shadow, the 45°-rotated tail square and its per-side border suppression). Popover is INFORMATIONAL and non-modal: arbitrary content, a close ×, and dismissing it means nothing. A Popconfirm has exactly two exits and DISMISSAL IS THE CANCEL, which is why it carries no close × — a × beside a Cancel button offers one outcome under two labels. THE TELL: if dismissing the thing has no consequence, it is a Popover.",
    "Modals": "A modal is interruptive — scrim, focus trap, the page stops. A Popconfirm is anchored to the object and the page keeps working around it; that is the itinerary's own wording, 'inline confirm-in-place'. Which actions may use which is a PRODUCT decision and is Dave's (see decisionsForDave 1). Nothing here licenses a Popconfirm for an irreversible money movement.",
    "Confirmation": "The end-of-flow success screen REPORTS an outcome after the fact; this asks BEFORE. Opposite ends of the same event. They share only the button pair, which is copied from it verbatim.",
    "Tooltip": "Hover/focus annotation, plain text, nothing to act on."
  },
  "props": [
    {
      "name": "tone",
      "type": "enum",
      "values": [
        "default",
        "danger"
      ],
      "default": "default",
      "binds": {
        "danger": "rag/error-ink"
      },
      "$note": "danger adds the warning glyph in the ink seat. ⛔ THE STORE HAS NO DESTRUCTIVE BUTTON SEAT — probed #204, there is no button/danger/*, button/destructive/* or button/critical/* in tokens/semantic-colour.json — and this component invents none. Weight is carried by the glyph (rag/error-ink, s151-D1's own two-red values, MONO ONLY), by the VERB in the confirm label, and by the question. Colour is the third channel, never the first.",
      "$status": "PROPOSED #204, Dave's eye owed"
    },
    {
      "name": "trigger",
      "type": "enum",
      "values": [
        "text",
        "icon-only"
      ],
      "default": "text",
      "$note": "The icon-only form is 44×44 exactly — the ruled minimum, enforced by hand because no gate reads the target token for hit area. Its accessible name names the OBJECT ('Remove Meridian Supplies'), not the mechanism.",
      "$status": "PROPOSED #204, Dave's eye owed"
    },
    {
      "name": "align",
      "type": "enum",
      "values": [
        "start",
        "end"
      ],
      "default": "start",
      "$note": "Which edge of the anchor the bubble hangs from. A stand-in for real space-aware placement, which is NOT re-drawn here — see the placement residual.",
      "$status": "PROPOSED #204, Dave's eye owed"
    },
    {
      "name": "body",
      "type": "boolean",
      "default": true,
      "$note": "The consequence sentence beneath the question. Optional: a low-stakes confirm in a dense row can be question-plus-actions only, and the third specimen shows that form.",
      "$status": "PROPOSED #204, Dave's eye owed"
    }
  ],
  "variants": [
    {
      "name": "default",
      "use": "a reversible action that still deserves a check — removing a payee, discarding a draft"
    },
    {
      "name": "danger",
      "use": "an action with a consequence the reader should read before confirming; the glyph takes the error ink and the confirm label repeats the verb"
    },
    {
      "name": "icon-in-row",
      "use": "a 44×44 icon trigger inside a list row, confirming beside the row rather than over it"
    }
  ],
  "tokens": {
    "surface": "background/default",
    "border": "elevation/border — transparent in light, the grey outline in dark; Popover's own elevation recipe",
    "shadow": "elevation/functional",
    "text": "text/default",
    "muted": "text/secondary",
    "page": "background/default",
    "focus": "focus/ring",
    "radius": "border-radius/surface (bubble) and border-radius/control (buttons) — 0, square; no exemption applies",
    "target": "target/min (44px) — bound in the manifest so the drift gate reads the value, then MEASURED in a real browser because no gate reads it for hit area",
    "actions": {
      "primary-bg": "button/primary/background/default",
      "primary-bg-hover": "button/primary/background/hover",
      "primary-label": "button/primary/label/default",
      "ghost-hover": "tertiary/background/hover"
    },
    "danger": {
      "glyph": "rag/error-ink — #DA1A00 on white, #F6604C elsewhere (s151-D1, the two-red law, MONO ONLY). Measured on this surface #204 with the repo's own _contrast_utils.contrast_ratio: 5.090 light, 5.550 dark."
    }
  },
  "$finding-no-destructive-seat": "⛔ THE TOKEN STORE HAS NO DESTRUCTIVE BUTTON SEAT. Probed #204: grep -inE 'danger|destructive|critical' over knowledge/tokens/semantic-colour.json returns NOTHING. Every button seat in the store is primary / secondary / tertiary / quaternary. A destructive confirm is the canonical place a design system reaches for a danger button, and this system does not have one — so the specimen does not invent one, and the destructive variant carries its weight through the glyph, the verb and the question instead. WHETHER ONE SHOULD EXIST IS DAVE'S AND IS NOT SETTLED HERE. It interacts directly with s151-D1 (the two-red law) and s149-D1 (the mono error ink camp, #1A1A1A on #F6604C), both of which are FIRM and neither of which is touched: nothing in this component paints text on an error fill, so the ink camp does not arise.",
  "$finding-role-vocabulary": "⛔ THE ROLE SHIPPED IS role=\"dialog\", AND THAT IS A GATE CONSTRAINT, NOT A DESIGN CHOICE. role=\"alertdialog\" is the semantically right role for a confirm-in-place and the component was built that way first. It drove _validate_a11y.py RED, verbatim: 'CTRL vocabulary: unknown ARIA role(s) [\"alertdialog\"] — this gate cannot classify them as interactive or structural'. The gate's vocabulary in knowledge/_a11y_target.py already carries BOTH 'alert' and 'dialog' in NON_INTERACTIVE_ROLES and is simply missing their compound. That file is a shared gate outside Lane M's fence and was NOT edited; the snippet fell back to role=\"dialog\" (the gated Popover's own role) so the tree stays green, and the one-line vocabulary addition is proposed to the BUILD-PM. A green gate here is measuring role=\"dialog\", not endorsing it.",
  "relationships": {
    "livesInside": [
      "Template — list or table screen",
      "Lock-up — payee row",
      "Data-grid row actions"
    ],
    "commonPatterns": [
      "remove an item from a list",
      "discard an unsaved draft",
      "revoke an access grant"
    ],
    "mustNotNeighbour": []
  },
  "accessibility": {
    "relatedSC": [
      "1.4.1",
      "1.4.3",
      "1.4.11",
      "2.1.2",
      "2.4.3",
      "2.4.7",
      "2.5.8",
      "3.2.1",
      "4.1.2"
    ],
    "role": "The bubble is role=\"dialog\" with aria-labelledby on the question and aria-describedby on the consequence sentence. The trigger carries aria-haspopup=\"dialog\", aria-expanded and aria-controls. See $finding-role-vocabulary: alertdialog is the intended role and is blocked on a gate vocabulary gap.",
    "focus": "Focus moves to the CONFIRM button on open — the affirmative is the reason the bubble exists, and the cancel is reachable by one Shift+Tab and by Escape. Focus returns to the trigger on every close. Tab is NOT trapped: leaving the bubble closes it, which is Popover's non-modal reading, inherited. ⚠ WHETHER A DESTRUCTIVE CONFIRM SHOULD TRAP IS AN OPEN QUESTION — see decisionsForDave 3.",
    "dismissal": "Escape cancels, an outside click cancels, re-activating the trigger cancels. Dismissal and cancel are the same outcome by design, which is why there is no close ×.",
    "colourIsNeverAlone": "The danger glyph is aria-hidden and says nothing a reader cannot also read: the question names the object, the body names the consequence, the confirm button repeats the verb. data-carries=\"symbol label\" is declared in markup so the rendering gate can check the carrier against real DOM. Dave is astigmatic and red is a problem hue — nothing here leans on it.",
    "targetSize": "Every interactive target is >= 44px (target/min), MEASURED in a real browser at 1400px and 480px across all four themes. No gate reads the target token for hit area."
  },
  "antiPatterns": [
    "Never give a Popconfirm a close ×. Dismissal here IS the cancel; a × offers the same outcome under a second label and teaches the reader that one of the two is something else.",
    "Never label the confirm button 'OK' or 'Yes'. It repeats the verb of the action — 'Remove payee', 'Delete standing order' — so a reader who has stopped reading the question still knows what they are agreeing to.",
    "Never use a Popconfirm where the reader cannot see what will change. If the object is off-screen, the anchor has stopped doing its job and the pattern should be a Modal.",
    "Never carry the destructive meaning in colour alone. There is no danger button seat in this system; the word does the work.",
    "Never nest a Popconfirm inside another overlay that already traps focus — the two dismissal models fight and Escape becomes ambiguous.",
    "REVIEW Never promote, gate or register this component without Dave's word. It is PROPOSED #204 and the role, the placement mechanism, the focus model and the permitted action class are all open."
  ],
  "tokenValidation": {
    "date": "2026-08-19",
    "against": "knowledge/tokens/semantic-colour.json + layout.json, resolved through _validate_snippets.resolve()",
    "result": "PASS — snippet gate rc=0, 0 failures repo-wide with this file present. Every declared var matches the store in BOTH modes. a11y gate rc=0. Type-composite gate rc=0 on this file; repo-wide 1097, unchanged — this file adds 0 to the shrink-only ratchet.",
    "declaredAbsence": "No rag-on-neutral FILL pair is declared. The only RAG value painted is rag/error-ink on background/default — the INK seat — and it IS declared and measured (5.090 light, 5.550 dark). The non-colour carrier is declared in markup as data-carries=\"symbol label\" per s151-D2 / s160-D2, so the rendering gate can check it against real DOM.",
    "notRun": "_validate_state_contrast.py was NOT run: a filtered run overwrites the tracked _STATE-CONTRAST-AUDIT.md and Lane M held no shared-file licence. Declared and owed to the BUILD-PM, not glossed.",
    "notRegistered": "Absent from knowledge/component-types.json (a shared file, outside the lane fence), so no press-physics AUTO-PARTIAL is injected and the pressables carry colour-only states — the same declared state the gated Popover shipped in.",
    "renderProof": "See the receipt at notes/_receipts/2026-08-19-204-wave-laneM-feedback-layout.md for the driven figures."
  },
  "provenance": {
    "source": "gap-report",
    "$note": "Itinerary row 81/75 (2026-07-14 sheet), row 75: 'Popconfirm — Inline confirm-in-place', Feedback & status, P2. Confirmed a TRUE gap at #204 by filename greps under every plausible alias, a content grep over knowledge/snippets and knowledge/components, and a direct grep of knowledge/_rulings.json (the store itself, not the retrieval index, which _capture_gate.py --selftest reports STALE). Built #204 Lane M from two gated parents (Popover, Confirmation), both untouched. No Figma node binds this component; provenance.figma_node stays empty until a design owner binds it."
  },
  "interactive": true,
  "stateModel": "full",
  "responsive": {
    "bubble": "max-width min(320px, 100vw - 32px) so it can never overflow a narrow viewport",
    "actions": "the pair stacks column-reverse and goes full width at <=480px (breakpoint/s) — Confirmation's own narrow behaviour, inherited",
    "$status": "PROPOSED #204, Dave's eye owed"
  },
  "dimensions": {
    "padding": 16,
    "gap": 8,
    "tailSize": 10,
    "glyph": 18,
    "buttonHeight": 44,
    "buttonMinWidth": 96,
    "iconTrigger": 44,
    "$note": "buttonHeight 44 and buttonMinWidth 96 are Confirmation's Button atom, unchanged. tailSize 10 is Popover's tail, unchanged. iconTrigger 44 is the ruled min-hit-area."
  },
  "$decisionsForDave": [
    "1 · WHICH ACTIONS MAY USE A POPCONFIRM AT ALL. Fintech semantics are yours. A confirm-in-place is right for removing a payee; it is probably wrong for sending money. Where is the line, and should the component's meta name it as a hard rule rather than guidance?",
    "2 · SHOULD A DESTRUCTIVE BUTTON SEAT EXIST? The store has none (probed, see $finding-no-destructive-seat). This specimen works without one. Adding one touches s151-D1 and s149-D1, both FIRM, and is not something a worker may propose into existence.",
    "3 · DOES A DESTRUCTIVE CONFIRM TRAP FOCUS? This inherits Popover's non-modal reading: no trap, leaving closes. The alternative reading is that a decision the page is waiting on should hold focus until it is made. One is not obviously right.",
    "4 · role=\"alertdialog\" or role=\"dialog\"? See $finding-role-vocabulary. The gate cannot currently express the former.",
    "5 · PLACEMENT. Popover owns a real space-aware placer; this anchors in flow so the open state renders statically. Should Popconfirm reuse Popover's placer (one mechanism, two components) or keep a simpler anchored form?",
    "6 · WHICH SIDE THE CONFIRM SITS ON. Cancel-then-confirm, left to right, is the specimen's order and it follows Confirmation's stacking. It is not ruled.",
    "7 · IS 'Popconfirm' THE NAME? It is the itinerary's word and a common one in other systems. It is not obviously the word this system would choose."
  ],
  "$copiedFrom": [
    "Popover (bubble chrome, dismiss + return-focus behaviour)",
    "Confirmation (the .btn primary/ghost action pair)",
    "Links (nothing — no link appears in this component)"
  ],
  "$stateModelNote": "'full' by schema enum (only 'simple' and 'full' are legal). The real model is open/closed with return-focus: Escape, outside click and re-activating the trigger all cancel, and focus returns to the trigger on every close."
}

{
  "name": "Coverage / runway bar",
  "category": "molecule",
  "purpose": "A READOUT that answers one question: does the money cover what is already scheduled, and until when? It states a verdict with a date, shows the arithmetic that produces it (balance − committed = buffer), and draws the split on a bar. ⚠ THE BAR IS A GATED Progress-bar, COPIED BYTE-FOR-BYTE — this component draws no new bar. What it adds is the verdict, the arithmetic and the legend. PROPOSED #204 (itinerary row 94, slug runway-bar) — NOT GATED, NOT RULED, AND ITS PROVENANCE IS A TEST FIXTURE (see provenance). Fintech semantics are Dave's (the Kpi-tile precedent, s182-D2).",
  "intent": "composition",
  "props": [
    { "name": "balance", "type": "number", "$note": "The domain maximum — aria-valuemax." },
    { "name": "committed", "type": "number", "$note": "The fill — aria-valuenow. ⚠ CLAMPED to balance in the SHORT state, because a progressbar cannot express overflow. The true figure appears in the legend, the arithmetic and aria-valuetext." },
    { "name": "buffer", "type": "number", "$note": "Derived: balance − committed. Rendered through the Amount-display money-format primitive (symbol before, no space, tabular lining, U+2212 minus, MONOCHROME)." },
    { "name": "verdict", "type": "string", "$note": "★ THE POINT OF THE COMPONENT. A WORD AND A DATE — 'Covered through 31 May', 'Covered to 24 May', 'Short from 12 May'. Never a colour on its own." },
    { "name": "verdictTone", "type": "enum", "values": ["ok", "warn"], "$note": "Renders the Status-indicator RAG-tint chip. ⛔ WHICH VERDICT MAPS TO WHICH TONE IS A SEMANTIC BINDING AND IS DAVE'S — proposed here, not ruled." },
    { "name": "showMath", "type": "boolean", "default": true, "$note": "The balance/committed/buffer definition list. Turning it off makes this a Progress bar (see antiPatterns)." },
    { "name": "size", "type": "enum", "values": ["default", "emphasis"], "default": "default", "$note": "4px and 8px rules — Progress-bar's own two sizes, same token pair, unchanged." }
  ],
  "variants": [
    { "name": "covered", "use": "Buffer positive. Bar under the full track." },
    { "name": "tight", "use": "Buffer nearly gone. Same anatomy, different numbers, different WORD — NOT a different colour." },
    { "name": "short", "use": "Committed exceeds balance. Bar pinned at 100%, shortfall shown as a signed figure and a date. ⛔ NO RED — see tokens.$note." },
    { "name": "emphasis", "use": "8px rule where the coverage is the primary content of its region. Progress-bar's .pb-lg size." }
  ],
  "tokens": {
    "fill": "progress/complete — theme INK in all four themes since s175-D1 (Mono/Console #1A1A1A | #FFFFFF, Legacy #333333 | #FFFFFF, Supercharge #13110E | #F7F6F4)",
    "track": "progress/incomplete — #F0F0F0 | #484848 in Mono/Console/Legacy; #DFDEDC | #413934 in Supercharge via the neutral→warm DNA rebind",
    "label": "text/default @ .t-cm-label",
    "figures": "text/default @ .t-cm-figure-4 (buffer, display size) / .t-cm-figure-6 (legend + arithmetic, tabular)",
    "muted": "text/secondary @ .t-cm-legal and .t-cm-caption",
    "border": "border/subtle — the buffer swatch outline and the arithmetic total rule",
    "verdict": "rag/success + rag/success-tint | rag/warning + rag/warning-tint — the Status-indicator chip, copied byte-for-byte from Account-card",
    "radius": "border-radius/indicator (resolves 0 in Mono — square, the angular rule; 4px in Console via the cascade)",
    "$note": "⛔⛔ NO GREEN/RED WAS INVENTED FOR THE BAR, AND THAT IS THE POINT. A cash-runway meter is exactly where a healthy/critical binding gets improvised. The bar is INK ON TRACK in every state INCLUDING 'short', inherited unchanged from the gated Progress-bar, whose meta gives the reason in Dave's own terms: 'Progress is STRUCTURE, not status (Dave 2026-07-21) — hence the ink pair rather than a RAG colour.' Coverage is a QUANTITY. The VERDICT is a separate object carrying a word and a date. NO NEW TOKEN IS WANTED OR MINTED."
  },
  "motion": {
    "entry": "The fill grows to its value — Progress-bar's transition, copied.",
    "hover": "None. Passive.",
    "reducedMotion": "Progress-bar's own clause copied: the fill still MOVES to its final position (the value must be reachable), it just arrives without an animated sweep. Global collapse also present.",
    "tokens": []
  },
  "responsive": {
    "rule": "Fluid to a 480px max-width column; the bar is width:100% of its container. Legend and head wrap. Verified at 1400px and 480px.",
    "tokens": []
  },
  "relationships": {
    "livesInside": ["Cash-flow / coverage dashboards", "Account overview", "Payment-run approval screens"],
    "mustNotNeighbour": ["A Chart-bullet of the same figures (pick one — and if you have a TARGET, the Chart-bullet is the right one)", "A bare Progress bar of the same figures (the readout already contains one)"],
    "commonPatterns": ["cash coverage for a scheduled payment run", "buffer after committed outgoings", "limits / allowance headroom"],
    "triggeredBy": []
  },
  "accessibility": {
    "role": "The readout is role=\"group\" + aria-labelledby. The bar is role=\"progressbar\" with aria-valuenow/valuemin/valuemax and a full aria-valuetext, copied from Progress-bar's non-percentage specimen.",
    "valueText": "aria-valuetext carries the whole sentence including the VERDICT AND THE DATE, so AT hears the answer, not just a ratio.",
    "openQuestion": "⚠ role=\"progressbar\" vs role=\"meter\" is OPEN and Dave's. progressbar is used because it is what the gated parent carries. THE SEARCH THAT FAILED TO SETTLE IT (s202-D3): `grep -rn 'role=\"meter\"' knowledge/snippets/` → 2 hits, BOTH of them the new snippet's own prose, i.e. ZERO in the 87 pre-existing snippets; `grep -icE '\\bmeter\\b' knowledge/_rulings.json` → 0. Nothing in the store rules it either way.",
    "notColourAlone": "Enforced THREE ways on every specimen: the verdict WORD (and date) in the chip, the full arithmetic in text at 17.4:1, and aria-valuetext on the bar. Strip every colour from this component and it still says everything it means (1.4.1).",
    "passive": "interactive:false throughout. No focus indicator, nothing in the tab order — so the 44px minimum hit area does not apply. Stated so the absence is DECLARED rather than assumed.",
    "math": "The arithmetic is a real <dl>, so the sum is in source order and readable by AT rather than being a visual arrangement.",
    "relatedSC": ["1.4.1 Use of Color", "1.4.11 Non-text Contrast", "1.3.1 Info and Relationships", "4.1.2 Name, Role, Value", "2.3.3 Animation from Interactions"]
  },
  "antiPatterns": [
    "⛔ COLOURING THE BAR RED WHEN COVERAGE IS SHORT, or green when it is healthy. Progress is structure, not status (Dave 2026-07-21, carried in progress-bar.meta). Coverage is a quantity. The verdict word and the date are the carriers.",
    "⛔ ADDING A TARGET MARKER. A bar with a target IS a Chart-bullet and should be one. This component has no target — it has a horizon.",
    "⛔ ADDING QUALITATIVE BANDS behind the bar. Same reason: those are Chart-bullet's qualitative ranges.",
    "Shipping the bar WITHOUT the verdict and the arithmetic. That is a Progress bar and should be one — the readout is the whole component.",
    "Rendering the verdict as a colour with no word or date.",
    "Using this for a MULTI-category composition (three or more segments). Two segments of one balance at one instant is a rule; more than that is Chart-donut or Chart-bar's stacked column.",
    "Using this for coverage OVER TIME. That is Chart-stacked-area.",
    "Letting aria-valuenow exceed aria-valuemax in the short state instead of clamping it and carrying the true figure in aria-valuetext.",
    "Relying on the verdict chip's DOT. It is 1.98:1 / 2.18:1 standalone (measured #204) — the inherited Account-card / Status-indicator finding."
  ],
  "tokenValidation": {
    "date": "2026-08-19",
    "against": "token store (semantic-colour.json) via #token-manifest",
    "result": "PROPOSED — gates run at #204 by the worker lane: _validate_snippets.py rc=0 (90 snippets, 0 failures), _validate_a11y.py rc=0 (90 snippets, 0 failures), _validate_type_composites.py filtered rc=0 and repo-wide 1097 violations UNCHANGED from the measured baseline (this file adds ZERO — it declares no raw font at all, following Progress-bar's zero-raw-type pattern). _validate_dataviz.py NOT APPLICABLE and declared: this component carries NO dataviz geometry, no SVG and no series token, which is itself part of the Chart-bullet adjudication. _validate_state_contrast.py NOT RUN and DECLARED OWED. Radius / icons / coverage and every generator --check are the BUILD-PM's serially. This is a PROPOSAL, not a proof-of-done.",
    "$note": "fill-on-track (progress/complete on progress/incomplete) clears 3:1 in ALL FOUR themes since s175-D1 — Mono/Console/Legacy 15.27 light / 9.15 dark, Supercharge 14.02 / 10.46 — Progress-bar's own recorded figures against canon/canon.css. It is NOT declared as a gated contrastPair here, for Progress-bar's own stated reason: the snippet gate resolves against tokens/semantic-colour.json, the MONO base only, and cannot see the other three legs. Meaning never rests on that boundary anyway."
  },
  "provenance": {
    "source": "gap-report",
    "$sourceNarrative": "⚠ PROVENANCE NARRATIVE, MOVED HERE BY THE #204 FIX SUB. It was authored into `provenance.source`, which meta.schema.json constrains to an enum of five values, so the file failed the schema. Nothing is deleted: the paragraph is preserved verbatim below and `provenance.source` now carries the enum value the paragraph itself describes — \"gap-report\" (a candidate surfaced by a journey/gap report, not yet reconciled to a Figma node or code path). ⛔ NOT A SCHEMA DECISION: whether meta.schema.json should gain a typed `provenance.note` field is OPEN TO DAVE per the #204 verifier receipt (every meta.schema.json amendment in the store's history was Dave's — s140-D1, s165-D5). `$`-prefixed keys are already legal everywhere by the schema's own patternProperties, so this move needs no amendment. VERBATIM ORIGINAL FOLLOWS ⇒ ⚠⚠ THIS ROW ORIGINATES IN A TEST FIXTURE, NOT A PRODUCT NEED — stated as the headline, not a footnote. Itinerary row 94's own note says 'Cash-runway meter (fitness tests invented this)', and the origin chain is PROVEN, not assumed. (1) knowledge/_COMPONENT-GAPS.md, under 'Token / system gaps (SME-Payments fitness tests, 2026-06-30) — Exposed by the portfolio run: the canon was silent in exactly the places it had to invent', records verbatim: 'Data-viz palette + chart primitives | no chart components, no named data series — the waterfall / RUNWAY / proportional bars WERE INVENTED'. (2) `grep -rn \"runway\" knowledge/_fitness-test/*.html` returns four synthetic pages (sme-payments-portfolio, -balanced, -final, cold-A-inference) each hand-rolling a .runway section in raw hex and raw font shorthands — probe artefacts, not product artefacts. (3) That logged gap was promoted into knowledge/_COMPONENT-LIBRARY-TARGET.md line 104, the 'Fintech-specific' table, GAP · P2–P3. (4) The target table became the itinerary row. (5) `grep -inE \"runway|coverage|burn rate|payment-card|fintech|plastic\" knowledge/_rulings.json` returns ZERO hits naming this component ('coverage' appears only as GATE coverage). (6) The retrieval index is STALE this session (_capture_gate.py --selftest says so), so the ruling claim rests on the DIRECT GREP of _rulings.json, the store itself, not on _memento_search.py. ⇒ There IS a real user question underneath — 'does my money cover what is already scheduled, and until when?' — and the fitness test answered it with drawn evidence. But NOBODY HAS RULED THAT IT SHOULD BE A COMPONENT. That is Dave's first decision. Measured a TRUE GAP by reviews/ITINERARY-STATUS-2026-08-19-v1.json (#203 Lane H): drift AGREES, no artefact under any alias (re-probed #204 under runway/coverage/meter/gauge/burn/cash across knowledge/snippets/ and knowledge/components/ — all empty).",
    "figma_node": "",
    "code_path": "knowledge/snippets/Runway-bar.reference.html"
  },
  "$differsFrom": {
    "Chart-bullet": "★ THE BRIEF'S FLAGGED NEIGHBOUR, AND THE ANSWER IS NO. Chart-bullet's own purpose line: 'a measure bar against a COMPARATIVE TARGET MARKER and QUALITATIVE PERFORMANCE RANGES', intent 'comparison', built as an SVG figure at a fixed 580px with a real <table class=\"dv-table\"> (dv-005), a data/series/1 measure fill and an ink target tick. A runway bar has NO target, NO bands, NO SVG, NO data table and NO dataviz series token. THE TELL: a Chart-bullet needs a TARGET; a runway bar has no target, it has a HORIZON — nothing is measured against a goal, the question is how far the money reaches. If you have a target, use Chart-bullet. This component must never grow one.",
    "Progress-bar": "★ THIS IS THE REAL PARENT, and it is not close, it is exact. Progress-bar's own commonPatterns already lists 'savings goal / LIMITS METER', and its third specimen is a non-percentage determinate bar ('Savings goal · 1,450 of 2,000') carrying its domain in aria-valuetext. Committed money on a track of total balance is that same shape. THE BAR IS COPIED BYTE-FOR-BYTE — .pb-track/.pb-fill, 4px and 8px, progress/complete on progress/incomplete, role and aria — AND NOTHING NEW WAS DRAWN AT THE BAR LEVEL. What this adds is the READOUT: the verdict-with-a-date, the balance-minus-committed arithmetic, and the two-key legend. A runway readout without those IS a Progress bar and should be one.",
    "Chart-donut / Chart-stacked-area": "Those are composition charts across MANY categories, or across TIME. This is ONE balance split into exactly TWO parts at ONE instant, and it is a rule, not a chart.",
    "Kpi-tile / Stat-card": "Those state a metric and its CHANGE (or the shape of the change) against a prior period. This states a FORECAST — a horizon date — from a balance and a schedule. There is no delta and no arrow anywhere in this component, which is also why it does not touch the live two-red arrow seam."
  },
  "$decisionsForDave": [
    "★ FIRST: should this component exist at all? It originates in a fitness-test fixture. Nothing in the store asked for it. Declining it is a completely legitimate answer and the itinerary row can be closed as 'not a component'.",
    "If it does exist: is the shape right? Verdict + buffer figure + bar + legend + arithmetic — or is that too much for one component and the arithmetic belongs in a Summary?",
    "★ The verdict vocabulary and its chip binding. 'Covered through 31 May' → success tint; 'Covered to 24 May' → warning tint; 'Short from 12 May' → warning tint. Should 'short' be the ERROR seat instead? That touches the two-red law and I deliberately did not take it.",
    "role=\"progressbar\" vs role=\"meter\" — nothing in the store rules it (searches quoted in accessibility.openQuestion).",
    "The SHORT state's clamped bar. Pinning at 100% is honest but silent about the overflow. Should there be a dedicated overflow treatment, and if so, what is it that is not a red bar?",
    "The legend's buffer swatch takes a 1px border/subtle outline so the track colour is visible against the page in light mode. That is a specimen choice, not a rule.",
    "Should the emphasis (8px) variant exist here, or should a consumer just compose Progress-bar's own emphasis size?"
  ]
}

{
  "name": "Tags input",
  "category": "molecule",
  "purpose": "A field the user types free values into, each committed as a removable chip. Use it where the vocabulary is the user's own — payment references, labels, search terms — and no list can be offered. The gated Tags atom is the display half of this: same chip, no field.",
  "$provenance-note": "NEW at #203 (wave 3b, lane J) against itinerary row 23 (P2, 'Free-entry token field'). Verified absent first-hand: Tags.reference.html EXISTS and is gated, but it is a display atom — grep for <input / contenteditable in it returns nothing, and its meta declares category 'atom' with variants tag and tag-link only. No tags-input snippet or meta existed under any slug.",
  "interactive": true,
  "props": [
    { "name": "max", "type": "number", "default": 8, "$status": "PROPOSED #203, Dave's eye owed — 8 is the reference's illustrative ceiling, not a ruled product limit." },
    { "name": "commitKeys", "type": "enum", "values": ["enter", "enter+comma"], "default": "enter+comma", "$note": "Comma is included because reference lists are habitually comma-separated; blur also commits a pending value rather than discarding it." },
    { "name": "state", "type": "enum", "values": ["default", "hover", "focus", "disabled", "error"], "default": "default", "$note": "Same state channel as Input-fields/Textarea — inherited." },
    { "name": "backspaceBehaviour", "type": "enum", "values": ["arm-then-remove", "remove-immediately"], "default": "arm-then-remove", "$status": "PROPOSED #203, Dave's eye owed. The first Backspace on an empty field ARMS the last chip (an inset outline, announced politely); a second removes it. Immediate removal loses data silently for fast typists, but two keystrokes is more work for everyone." }
  ],
  "variants": [
    { "name": "with tags", "use": "The working state — chips wrap inside the field and the counter reports how many remain." },
    { "name": "empty", "use": "A plain one-row field, so it never looks broken before use; the help text states how a value is committed." }
  ],
  "tokens": {
    "field-background": "form/background/default (transparent), hover form/background/hover",
    "field-border": "form/border/default; focus-within form/border/active + a 4px inset bottom stroke; disabled form/border/disabled; refusal a 4px inset rag/error stroke (dark: full rag/error border)",
    "chip": "INHERITED FROM TAGS — 1px form/border/default on transparent, border-radius/control, label text/default, dismiss glyph icon/default. No new chip tokens.",
    "chip-armed": "a 1px inset rule in form/border/active on the chip Backspace is about to take — an outline change, never colour alone",
    "text": "text/default; disabled text/disabled",
    "counter": "text/default at .t-cm-legal; the approaching-limit signal is the WORDING, not a weight or a colour",
    "focus": "focus/ring",
    "shape": "border-radius/control (field and chip)",
    "hit-area": "target/min (44px) on the field row. Chip dismiss 24px — the gated Tags value, inherited unchanged."
  },
  "relationships": {
    "livesInside": ["Form", "Filter bar", "Dialog"],
    "mustNotNeighbour": [],
    "commonPatterns": ["free-entry token field", "payment reference list", "label editor"]
  },
  "accessibility": {
    "roles": "A plain text input — deliberately NOT role=combobox, because there is no list to expand and claiming one would be a lie to AT. Each chip's dismiss is a real button with a purposeful accessible name ('Remove INV-4471').",
    "keyboard": "Enter or comma commits; blur commits a pending value; Backspace on an empty field arms the last chip and a second Backspace removes it; each dismiss button is tabbable.",
    "announcements": "A polite live region announces every add, every removal, the armed chip, and each refusal — the chip list changes outside the caret's reading position, so silence would be a data loss the user cannot perceive.",
    "states": "Refusals set aria-invalid + aria-describedby on the input and render a message that pairs a symbol with words and stays ink. Duplicates and the limit are refused explicitly, never silently dropped.",
    "targetArea": "Field row 44px; chip dismiss 24px (WCAG 2.5.8 minimum), inherited from Tags and flagged rather than silently raised.",
    "relatedSC": ["1.3.1", "1.4.1", "1.4.11", "2.1.1", "2.4.7", "2.5.8", "3.3.1", "4.1.2", "4.1.3"],
    "$sc-note": "3.3.3 Error Suggestion genuinely applies (the refusals tell the user what to do), but it is NOT in the KNOWN_SC compliance lookup _build_integrity.py reads, and that lookup is a shared file this lane may not edit. Declared here rather than dropped silently — PROPOSED for the conductor: add 3.3.3 to the lookup."
  },
  "antiPatterns": [
    "Dropping a duplicate or an over-limit value silently. A refusal the user cannot see is indistinguishable from a bug.",
    "Discarding a half-typed value on blur. It is committed instead — the user typed it on purpose.",
    "Drawing a second chip. This is the Tags chip; changes belong in Tags.",
    "Claiming role=combobox without a list. There are no options here; announcing a collapsed listbox that never opens is worse than plain input semantics.",
    "Signalling 'nearly at the limit' with colour or weight. The wording carries it — colour alone fails 1.4.1 and weight would need a raw font declaration TYPE-002 forbids."
  ],
  "tokenValidation": {
    "date": "2026-08-19",
    "against": "knowledge/tokens/semantic-colour.json via _validate_snippets.py (MONO base only)",
    "result": "PASS — 15 declared vars resolve in both light and dark; 5 declared contrast pairs clear their thresholds in both modes (snippet gate rc=0).",
    "$scope": "MONO base only. The other three themes are shown, not measured, in reviews/REVIEW-203-tags-input-four-themes-v1.html.",
    "$deprecated": "No deprecated tokens bound. The OUTLINED Tags chip is used, which is already rebound onto form/*; the filled-chip deprecation recorded in tags.meta.json is not inherited.",
    "$notGenerated": "canon.css carries NO .cn-tags-input scope yet — no generator was run by this lane (Lane G owns that surface at #203)."
  },
  "provenance": {
    "source": "gap-report",
    "figma_node": "",
    "code_path": "",
    "$note": "Itinerary row 23. Mine-from named in the brief: Ant / Untitled. No Figma node; the chip comes from the gated Tags node (413:10962) via the Tags snippet."
  },
  "edges": {
    "renderedBy": [{ "ref": "snippet:Tags-input.reference.html" }],
    "containedBy": [{ "ref": "component:tags", "$note": "shares the Tags chip, copied not re-drawn" }],
    "commonPattern": [{ "ref": "pattern:free-entry-token-field" }]
  }
}

{
  "name": "Timeline",
  "category": "organism",
  "$status": "PROPOSED #203, Dave's eye owed",
  "purpose": "The passive, ordered record of things that have already happened, where the time axis IS the structure: a vertical rail threading date-grouped entries, newest first. Two forms from one grammar — transaction history (status node + amount, the fintech case the itinerary names) and activity feed (actor avatar + what they did).",
  "$differsFromNeighbours": {
    "$why": "Three gated components already sit close to this one, and a reader will otherwise reach for the wrong one. Stated here because the brief requires a new component to say how it differs from its gated siblings.",
    "vs List-items (Transaction row, GATED)": "List-items is an INTERACTIVE, UNORDERED list — every row is a <button> with hover/pressed/disabled/processing states — and it answers 'which transaction do I want to open?'. Timeline is PASSIVE and ORDERED (<ol>), carries no press states, and answers 'what happened, in what order?'. The tell: remove the ordering from a Timeline and it becomes meaningless; remove it from List-items and nothing is lost. Where a feed genuinely needs each entry to open a detail view, the correct answer is List-items inside a date group — NOT a Timeline that grows buttons. The RAG chip and avatar atoms here are List-items' own, copied verbatim.",
    "vs Progress-tracker (GATED, display-only)": "Visually the closest, and the one most likely to be mistaken for this. Progress-tracker shows a KNOWN, FINITE, FORWARD process with done/current/upcoming steps and a completion the user is travelling toward; it carries aria-current=\"step\" and role=\"progressbar\". Timeline has no current step, no upcoming, no completion and no total — it is open-ended and backward-looking. The rail MECHANISM (li::before connector + node) is Progress-tracker's, rotated to vertical; the SEMANTICS are deliberately not inherited.",
    "vs Notifications (GATED, persistent)": "Notifications are messages awaiting the user's action. A Timeline entry is a record of something already done; it asks nothing."
  },
  "props": [
    { "name": "form", "type": "enum", "values": ["history", "activity"], "default": "history",
      "$note": "history = status node + amount (transaction history); activity = actor avatar + what they did (activity feed). One grammar, two node treatments.",
      "$status": "PROPOSED #203, Dave's eye owed" },
    { "name": "status", "type": "enum", "values": ["none", "ok", "warn", "err", "inf"], "default": "none",
      "binds": { "ok": "rag/success", "warn": "rag/warning", "err": "rag/error", "inf": "rag/information" },
      "$note": "Colours the rail node AND the entry's status chip. The chip always carries a WORD, so the dot never carries meaning alone (s151-D1 clause 4).",
      "$status": "PROPOSED #203, Dave's eye owed" },
    { "name": "grouped", "type": "boolean", "default": true,
      "$note": "Date group headings ('Today, 19 August'). Ungrouped is legal for short feeds but loses the axis the component exists for.",
      "$status": "PROPOSED #203, Dave's eye owed" }

Unmeasured: system prompt, memory index, tool output, transcripts, and the session's own writing — including three long commit messages. **Honest total ~40–50K tape, ESTIMATE, and the harness half is unreachable (`ds-025`).** ⚠ **`cl100k` is OpenAI's tokenizer, not Claude's — every figure here is a PROXY** (P3, raised by Dave this window).

(i) treated an uncontrolled n=1 observation's agreement with a 35-open-weight-model study as corroboration, when the gauge had plausibly primed the observation · (ii) proposed a behavioural fix ("then stop") to a structural problem.
- **outcome: 🟡 ruled + part-enacted.** Compactable BLOCK withdrawn (Dave), enacted + verified. Three lanes reconciled and committed. Friday brief written. ⬛ **2f NOT RUN and the ritual is PART-DONE — see the HOLE below.**

**HOLE #38 — ⛔ WITHDRAWN WITHIN THE HOUR, BY THE GATE, AND THE WITHDRAWAL IS THE ENTRY.** Declared above because `ds-022` reported *"session #38 left NO block and NO hole line"* and #39's greps for §C strata keys returned nothing on the format tried. **#39 hedged rather than asserted** — the [[gap-in-record-vs-gap-in-evidence]] discipline #38 itself established — writing *"possibly NOT a hole in the evidence; #38's post-mortem may exist in GM §C under a key #39 failed to match."* ★ **It does.** The very next gate run said so out loud: *"the newest §C stratum key says #38."* ⇒ **#38's GAUGE-LOG half was missing and its GM §C half was there all along** — the 2f split failing on one side, **which is precisely the failure #38 discovered about #35, one session later, with the roles reversed.** ★★ **THE LESSON IS NOT "check before declaring" — #39 did check. It is that AN UNMATCHED GREP IS NOT AN ABSENCE, and the honest move when a probe comes back empty is to hedge the claim rather than round it to a hole.** Had this been asserted flat, #40 would have rolled a recoverable record as lost. ⬛ **NO HOLE STANDS FOR #38.** What is actually missing is only its gauge-log block, now supplied by this line.

**HOLE #39 — 2f not run by this session either, and it is DECLARED not slipped.** The wrap closed with `31 in scope · 3 fail`: banner-region block (cut back, cleared), and two `ds-022` continuity fails that both trace to the missing #38 stratum. **#39 chose to commit the durable record — ruling, brief, ledger, three lane receipts — rather than half-do a roll it could not verify.** ⬛ **OWED AT #40, in order:** resolve `HOLE #38` (check GM §C first) → `_gm_move.py --ops roll_2f` → `_LIVE-STATE.md` ⏱ delta → the tape/bill pair → the #37 and #39 dossiers. **Nothing is lost: the arc is in `notes/_MEMENTO-DECISIONS.md` § ★ #39, the Friday brief, and commits `58556af` `e1649fb` `5e783bc` + this wrap's.**

#### 2026-07-29 #40 — descriptor NOT RECORDED by #40; key added retroactively

⚠ **THE KEY IS THE WHOLE ADDITION — nothing below it is new, moved, or reworded.** The three entries that follow (`tape/bill PAIR #40`, `META #40`, `META #40 (second)`) are #40's own, written in this file at its wrap. What #40 never wrote was this `#### <date> #<N>` line, so `STRATA_KEY_RE` could not see them and `ds-022` reported a session that had in fact testified — the state #41 raised as **PRESENT BUT UNKEYED** and declined to call a `HOLE`, correctly, because `HOLE` is a positive claim and would have been false. ⇒ **#41's refusal was right; the diagnosis was not. This is a filing error, not a gap, and a filing error is repaired by keying rather than by minting a fifth vocabulary term** — a term meaning *"we did not file it"* is the one that decays into `HOLE`'s meaning, which line 200 of `_capture_gate.py` already warns against. ⚠ **THE ROW IS PARTIAL AND STAYS PARTIAL:** #40 published no band, no fill and no self-reported error count, and #43 does not supply them. ⛔ **#38 IS NOT THE SAME CASE AND WAS NOT KEYED.** Three probes at #41 (§ `META #41`) found no #38 pre-flight or closed-band line anywhere in this file; its row lives in `GOOD-MORNING.md` §C alone. #39's *"now supplied by this line"* is a claim about the HOLE's status, **not** about #38's measurement — misread as discharge by #40, repeated to Dave by #41, and repeated a third time by #43 before this probe caught it. **Moving #38's row here is `roll_2f`, which the chronological guard correctly refuses; keying an empty heading would forge the dataset.** [born #43 · guards: this line · until: #38 is rolled or Dave rules otherwise]

**tape/bill PAIR #40 (ds-021 (c) — the standing per-wrap log entry, OWED since #39 and discharged here).** Measured post-wrap with `tiktoken cl100k_base`, on the finished files, **not by arithmetic** (#38's lesson: *a sum is not a measurement*): `GOOD-MORNING.md` **17,084 tape → ~26,822 bill** · `_LIVE-STATE.md` **20,076 tape → ~31,519 bill** · corpus **37,160 tape / ~58,341 bill**. ⚠ **The bill figures are DERIVED through `TAPE_TO_BILL = 1.57`, not measured — the ratio is still PROVISIONAL (n=2 real pairs) and this entry does not advance n, because no true `bill` reading is observable from inside a window (`ds-025`).** ⚠ **`cl100k` is OpenAI's tokenizer, not Claude's** — every figure here is a PROXY (P3, raised by Dave #39).

**⛔ META #40 — `roll_2f` FOR #38 IS MECHANICALLY IMPOSSIBLE, AND THIS FILE IS WHY.** #40 ran the supported path and the mover refused: `✖ notes/_GAUGE-LOG.md already carries blocks for [39], all later than #38 — appending would break the chronological contract this file declares in its own header (#27's defect)`. **The guard is correct and must not be worked around.** How it arose: **#39 wrote its own `#### 2026-07-29 #39` block while #38's stratum was still un-rolled in `GOOD-MORNING.md` §C**, so the log ran ahead of the file it is rolled from. ★ **#39's own owed-list names `_gm_move.py --ops roll_2f` as its second step — an instruction its author had already made unexecutable, in the same wrap.** ⇒ **the record can instruct a move the tooling forbids, and nothing detects the contradiction until a session tries it.** ⬛ **FORKED TO DAVE, not resolved by #40:** the log half is arguably already discharged by addition (`HOLE #38` above says *"what is actually missing is only its gauge-log block, now supplied by this line"*), the mover refuses a half-roll by contract, and hand-prepending is precisely #27's defect. **Consequence, declared: `ds-022` continuity stays RED and GM §C carries TWO stratum blocks (#38 and #40) instead of one.** Neither is drift; both are the blocked roll, visible on purpose.

**⛔ META #40 (second) — GM HAS DOUBLED IN SIX DAYS, AND THE MAXIMUM IS THE ANTI-GROWTH COMMIT.** Raised by **DAVE, unprompted** (*"GM looks big again, pfff. we had it at 9k at one point, this is a massive issue"*) and **confirmed to the commit**: `00abdf3` 2026-07-23 = **9,274 tape**; working tree at #40 = **18,433**. ★★ **All-time max 26,323 is `113eefc` — *"GM growth contracts, phase 1"* — the file has never been bigger than in the commit that wrote the rules against it growing.** Since that day's cut to 13,200, sessions #33–#40 ran the programme continuously and the file went **13,200 → 18,433, +40%**. ⚠ **The honest qualifier: the doubling is in the RETRIEVAL surface, NOT cold start** — the read chain is **3,837 tape, under its 4,500 warn and the smallest in three sessions** (#33's cut is holding). ⬛ **The cost no gate can see is that a HUMAN reads this file, and the complaint came from him.** Full evidence + reproducible method: `notes/_receipts/2026-07-29-gm-size-history-measurement.md`.

records.head: 2026-07-29 #41 — Opus solo, Dave live
records.text:
#### 2026-07-29 #41 — Opus solo, Dave live

- **band: ⛔ REFUSED — FIFTH consecutive session.** `_context_gauge.py:27` hardcodes `DEFAULT_WINDOW = 200_000`; Opus 5's window is **1M**. The same fill reads **~50% (AMBER, at the line)** on one denominator and **~10% (GREEN)** on the other, so a colour here would be invented, not measured ([[measuring-tool-must-not-guess]]). ⚠ **The denominator is now the single largest unresolved defect in this instrument** — five sessions have declined to name a band and none has been able to fix it, because fixing it is a ruling.
- **fill: PART-MEASURED, disk half ~45,800 tape** (`cl100k`, tiktoken installed and verified). Breakdown, so the estimate half is visible: files read/written **23,995 MEASURED** · boot (`MEMORY.md` + skill descriptions) **~10,200 MEASURED (#37/#38)** · ~22 bash calls **~9,000 ESTIMATE**. **Harness half UNOBSERVABLE** (`ds-025`) — system prompt, transcript, own replies. ⚠ `cl100k` is OpenAI's tokenizer, not Claude's — a PROXY (P3).
- **★★ tape/bill PAIR #41 — AND IT IS A REAL ONE, WHICH THIS LOG HAS NEVER HELD.** `ds-025` records that *"no true `bill` reading is observable from inside a window"*, and `ds-021(c)`'s n has been stuck at **2** because of it. **That premise is PART-FALSIFIED: the `Read` tool publishes what it charged.** Measured this window on `GOOD-MORNING.md` lines 1–321: **28,653 charged** against **13,548 tape** for the string *as the harness rendered it* (raw 12,333 + **1,215** of line-number prefixes, computed rather than waved at) ⇒ **2.11×**. Against `TAPE_TO_BILL = 1.57` that is a **1.35× under-statement of every `bill` figure in every banner and every entry in this file**, including #40's pair one screen above. ⬛ **NOT A RE-DIAL — n=1, one file, one tool, and the rendering is not byte-identical to the source.** Re-dialling `TAPE_TO_BILL` is **Dave's**; `ds-023` is the standing case for an agent promoting a number because it noticed one. **What this entry does is give the dataset its first honest row of the kind it was built for.**
- **self-reported errors: 2** — FIFTEENTH consecutive session, and both are the read-the-record class. (i) **The opener read `GOOD-MORNING.md` whole — 28,653 for a 3,838-tape contract.** It is what made the defect measurable, but it was not chosen; it was the default behaviour of `Read`. (ii) **Relayed #39's *"now supplied by this line"* to Dave as fact**, when that sentence is about the HOLE's status and not about #38's measurement — **an unchecked PRESENCE claim, the mirror of [[unmatched-grep-is-not-an-absence]]**, and it had already propagated through #40's fork before I repeated it.
- **outcome: 🟢 shipped + reframed.** `_CHAIN.md` built, wired, selftested (12 bites) and committed; cold start **19,405 → 4,374 tape, 77%**. #40's orphaned wrap verified and landed. 2f's purposes separated on Dave's question. ⬛ **`ds-022` STAYS RED and the strata stack is now THREE (#38, #40, #41)** — the count fail widens while the cause is unchanged, because `roll_2f` for #38 is still refused by the chronological guard. **Declared, not slipped.**

**⛔ META #41 — THE 2f ROLL HAS TWO PURPOSES AND THEY HAVE OPPOSITE ANSWERS.** Raised by **DAVE, in four words** — *"why should the stratum retire?"* — after two sessions had treated the roll as a given. The runbook states both: **(1) compaction** (GM-D5a, ruled **2026-07-27**: strata accumulate under §C with no roll rule, *"the author felt the pressure to roll and no rule licensed the move"*) and **(2) the dataset** (*"post-mortems → `notes/_GAUGE-LOG.md`… These are measurements, not narrative: pre-flight estimate vs closed band, overrun and its cause. The throttle programme keeps reasoning from n=1; the log is what makes it a countable dataset"*). ⛔ **PURPOSE 1 IS DEAD, AND A DATE KILLED IT:** #33 cut the read chain on **2026-07-28**, the day after GM-D5a was ruled. §C is retrieval surface and is never paid at cold start; `_CHAIN.md` made that true in the tool this window. ★ **This is #38's own finding — *"the cap is aimed at cold-start cost and #33 cut the chain out from under it"* — pointed at the ROLL RULE instead of the CAP, and nobody noticed it applied here too.** [[premise-ages-faster-than-rule]], second surface. ✅ **PURPOSE 2 IS THE WHOLE REASON, and it is unserved.** Three probes, named so the negative is checkable: no `#### <date> #38` key in this file · no #38 pre-flight/closed-band line · all **13** occurrences of `#38` are prose about other sessions. ⇒ **#38's row exists ONLY in `GOOD-MORNING.md` §C, and the cost of not rolling is not a bigger file — it is a dataset that still cannot answer the question it was built for.** ⬛ **FORKED TO DAVE, RESHAPED NOT RESOLVED: the mover does both jobs or neither, so an obsolete half is blocking a necessary one.** Three questions, none of them ruled here: does the roll still need to move anything out of §C · should `_gm_move.py` be able to do the dataset half alone · **is the chronological contract over-strict for a date-keyed dataset a parser sorts anyway?** (It exists because #27 hand-prepended; **order is file hygiene, not an analytical requirement** — and if it relaxes, #38's block simply appends at EOF and the blockage evaporates.) ⚠ **A FOURTH CORRECTION-AT-SOURCE in this chain:** #39's *"what is actually missing is only its gauge-log block, now supplied by this line"* is a claim about the HOLE's status; #40 read it as the measurement being discharged, and #41 repeated it to Dave before checking.

**⛔ META #41 (second) — #40's TESTIMONY EXISTS AND THE GATE CANNOT SEE IT, AND `HOLE` WOULD BE A LIE.** `ds-022` now fails with *"session #40 left NO block and NO hole line… declare it: `HOLE #40 — <why>`."* ⚠ **I am declining to write that line, and the refusal is the entry.** #40 wrote **both** halves of its testimony: a keyed `#### 2026-07-29 #40` stratum in `GOOD-MORNING.md` §C, and — in THIS file, two screens up — the `tape/bill PAIR #40` entry plus `META #40` and `META #40 (second)`. **What it did not write is a `#### <date> #40` KEY.** ⇒ **the testimony is present and the parser is blind to it.** ★ **`HOLE` is a POSITIVE CLAIM that we know the gap is there** (#37's framing, and the reason the marker was worth having); writing one here would forge exactly the dataset the throttle is re-derived from, and would repeat #39's `HOLE #38` error *knowingly* rather than by accident — [[unmatched-grep-is-not-an-absence]], now with the absence disproved in advance. ⬛ **A FIFTH STATE THE VOCABULARY LACKS, RAISED NOT MINTED.** The terms are `block` · `HOLE` · `ABSENT`; there is no term for **PRESENT BUT UNKEYED**. #37 raised the mid-flight-handover gap as the fourth and Dave ruled `HOLE` for it *because it invents nothing* — that reasoning does not transfer, because here `HOLE` invents something false. **Minting the term is Dave's** (`ds-023` is the standing case for an agent doing it because it noticed). ⚠ **CONSEQUENCE, DECLARED: `ds-022` stays RED, the strata stack stands at THREE (#38, #40, #41), and `roll_2f` remains refused for #38 by the chronological guard.** None of it is drift; all of it is one blocked mechanism, visible on purpose. ★ **And this is the second time in one window that the 2f machinery has produced a state its own vocabulary cannot name — which is itself evidence for the reframe in `META #41` above: the roll is doing two jobs, and the strain shows at the seam.**

**⛔ META #41 (third) — THE COMMIT SCRIPT EXISTS AND I COMMITTED FROM MEMORY THREE TIMES.** Raised by **DAVE**: *"can you run the commit runbook, maybe we are getting somewhere."* `knowledge/_git_commit.sh --reconciled <msgfile>` was **ruled 2026-07-26** and its own header states the evidence it was built on: *"3 of 5 commit-running sessions reconstructed the clear·stage·clear·commit·clear sequence from memory under wrap-time heat and hit the lock failure first."* ★ **#41 is 4 of 6, three times in one window** — and then reported the recurring lock warnings to Dave as *"standing sandbox behaviour, not an incident."* **It was not sandbox behaviour. It was the unrun script.** Four defects, all self-caught only because Dave asked: **(1)** script never called · **(2)** msgfiles at `/tmp/cmsg.txt`, `/tmp/c2.txt`, `/tmp/c3.txt` — the runbook says *never a fixed `/tmp` name*, the rule that exists because 2026-07-22 silently inscribed **the previous session's message** across 43 files; the message was read back each time, so the mitigation held **by luck of sequence, not by design** · **(3)** `index.lock` **left stranded** — a `git status` was run AFTER the clear, and step 4 requires the clear to be the last git-touching action; **that would have blocked GitHub Desktop when Dave went to push** · **(4)** the hand-rolled verification was **inverted**: `find .git -name '*.lock' && echo present` always takes the true branch because **`find` exits 0 on no matches**, so it reported a lock that was not there. The script's `| grep -q .` is correct. ★★ **THIS IS THE SESSION'S OWN FINDING IN DIFFERENT CLOTHES.** `_CHAIN.md` exists because *the chain was cut on paper and never in the tool*; the commit sequence is **mechanised in a script and was performed in prose**. ⇒ **A CORRECT PROCEDURE STORED WHERE THE HOT AGENT DOES NOT HAVE TO PASS THROUGH IT IS NOT A PROCEDURE — it is documentation.** The difference is that this one already had its generator, ruled three days ago, sitting unused. ⬛ **RAISED FOR DAVE, not ruled: nothing makes calling the script mandatory.** Options, unpicked: a capture-gate check that the wrap's commits carry the script's signature · a `--reconciled` receipt line in the stratum · leave it prose and accept the rate. ⚠ **`_to_delete/` is at 840K** — host-side `rm -rf _to_delete/*` when Dave is next at the machine (runbook 4b; the sandbox cannot).

**⛔ CORRECTION AT SOURCE, same window — THE COUNT ABOVE IS WRONG AND THE TRUE NUMBER IS WORSE.** `META #41 (third)` says *"#41 is 4 of 6"*. **It is 5 of 7.** #36 already made it 4 of 6 — and I did not know, because **#36's recurrence was never inscribed in this repo.** Two named probes: *(A)* the distinctive #36 diagnosis string (`starts RECALLING` / `stops READING the record`) → **zero hits corpus-wide**; *(B)* the commit-session count → **only two hits, `_RUNBOOK-git-commit.md:19` and `_git_commit.sh:5`, both still reading the ORIGINAL `3 of 5` from 2026-07-26.** ⇒ **the repo's count has never been updated and #36's instance is absent from it entirely.** ★★ **AND #36'S DIAGNOSIS IS THE SHARPEST THING IN THIS WHOLE THREAD, so its absence is the real defect — Dave named the mechanism at the time: *"and that's why pushing the context past 60 hits."*** ⇒ **the degradation past 60 has a SHAPE, not just a severity: an agent stops READING the record and starts RECALLING it** — the exact failure this project exists to prevent, arriving through the budget rather than through the corpus. ⇒ **the 45–60 band is not comfort; it is the range in which retrieval-not-recall still actually happens.** ⬛ **WHY IT WAS MISSABLE, and this is the finding:** it lived **only in a memory file**, whose own closing line reads *"(Not yet in the repo record — #36 closed over it deliberately, Dave's call; #37 to inscribe.)"* **#37, #38, #39 and #40 all passed and none inscribed it.** ★ **This is the trust hierarchy's own rule violated by the rule about violating it: *never let a durable rule live only on a Polaroid.*** Memory accelerates; the repo is the record — and a lesson about failing to read the record was filed where the record is not. **Inscribed here, five sessions late.** ⚠ **`_RUNBOOK-git-commit.md:19` and `_git_commit.sh:5` corrected to `5 of 7` in this same commit — a count that justifies a tool's existence and understates its own evidence is the [[assertion-propagation-gap]] class.**

Copied to §C·4 as opens **7, 8, 9** — Dave's SIX is now NINE. ★ **Fifth consecutive wrap the check has bitten, and the largest catch of the five.**

**META #42 (second) — `_gen_chain.py --check` RETURNED ONE UNREPRODUCED `STALE`.** At cold sandbox start, on a clean tree at HEAD, `--check` reported the chain did not match GM/LS. Regeneration produced a **byte-identical** file (`diff` empty, `git status` clean), and `--check` has been green on every subsequent run with `tiktoken` present. ⚠ **A BLOCKING build step reported a stale record and cannot be made to do it again.** Recorded because an unreproduced misfire in a gate is still a fact about the gate — not diagnosed, and no cause is proposed.

**ERRORS #42 — three, sixteenth consecutive session.** ★ **Stranded `.git/index.lock` by running `git status` AFTER `_git_commit.sh`'s final clear** — defect (3) of `e92ea0e`, a commit I had read in full one step earlier; it would have blocked Dave's GitHub Desktop push. Cleared as the last git-touching action. **Reading a procedure is not passing through it — the session's inherited lesson, re-learned at cost.** · Priced the opening job as *"the record is three commits behind HEAD"* when the evidence half was present all along; checking the other half shrank it. · Ran a §C probe whose `sed` range matched nothing and nearly read its zeros as absences ([[unmatched-grep-is-not-an-absence]]); caught by checking the heading format before asserting.

**HOLE #52 — the session wrote no stratum.** #52 spent its window on the 22-ruling decision pack and
closed without a `#### <date> #52` block. **A positive claim, not an absence:** the block was never
written, and this line says so rather than leaving the dataset to guess.

**HOLE #53 — the session wrote no stratum, deliberately, and the reason is the stack itself.** 2f has
not run for thirteen sessions and `GOOD-MORNING.md` carries **twelve** stratum blocks against a
contract of one. Adding a thirteenth to satisfy the form would have made the breach worse in order to
look compliant. ⚠ **#51 is NOT a hole and is not marked as one: its stratum EXISTS, in GM, unrolled.**
Writing `HOLE #51` would have made this log read complete at the price of an invented fact — the exact
move the ds-022 three-states ruling exists to forbid.

**META #53 — THE BLOCKER IS RULED AND UNENACTED, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS A DECLARATION AND NOT A FAILURE.**
`_gm_move.py::roll_2f` refuses a key later than the one being rolled (the chronological contract).
**Dave ruled that contract RELAXED at #52 (D5 (a)) — order was file hygiene, never an analytical
requirement, and a parser sorts the dataset anyway.** The enactment is one guard removed. ⇒ **Next
session: relax it, then roll all twelve in one pass.** ★ The cost of not doing it is now visible and
countable rather than felt: twelve blocks, thirteen sessions, one gate red throughout.

**★★★ META #53 (second) — D1 SETTLES WHAT THIS LOG HAS BEEN MEASURING.** Every band, cap and price in
this dataset is denominated in `tape` (`cl100k`, OpenAI's). **MEASURED this session against
`count_tokens()`: ×1.559 aggregate over five registers.** `TAPE_TO_BILL`, the ×1.57 this project
derived from n=2 observed pairs and held PROVISIONAL for nine sessions, **agrees to 0.7%.** ⇒ **the
`bill` half of the vocabulary was never a second quantity — it was the tokenizer, measured through a

#### META — UNKEYED #40 #41 #42: THE FOURTH STATE, RULED BY DAVE AT #54

**RAISED AT #41, OPEN THIRTEEN SESSIONS, SETTLED THIS WINDOW.** The state: a session whose testimony
EXISTS but which never wrote a `#### <date> #<N>` key, so the parser is blind to it. `HOLE` would be
a forgery — it is a POSITIVE claim of absence and the evidence was two screens up. The vocabulary
had `block` · `HOLE` · `ABSENT` and no fourth term, so #41 declined to write anything and forked it.

⬛ **DAVE'S RULING (#54): GATE IT SHUT, AND MARK THE THREE.** ★ Not a standing fourth term. The state
is an artefact of *testimony* and *key* being two separate acts — so the wrap is gated to make it
UNREACHABLE going forward, and only the sessions that already reached it get a name. **A vocabulary
term for a state that should not be possible is a permanent tax; prevention is not.**

- **UNKEYED #40** — testimony HERE in § `tape/bill PAIR #40`, `META #40`, `META #40 (second)`;
  stratum live in `GOOD-MORNING.md` §C. Key added retroactively (see its own descriptor line).
- **UNKEYED #41** — testimony HERE in § `META #41`, `META #41 (second)`; stratum live in GM §C.
- **UNKEYED #42** — testimony in the GM §C stratum; key added retroactively.

⚠ **THESE THREE ARE NOT ROLLED AND MUST NOT BE.** `roll_2f`'s duplicate-key guard refuses them
because this file already carries their keys, and it is RIGHT to: rolling would write one session's
record into this file twice, which is the harm the guard's own message names. **#54 rolled the other
NINE — #38 #43 #44 #46 #47 #48 #49 #50 #51 — and left these three stacked in GM deliberately.**

★★ **THE PATCH WAS THE PROBLEM, AND IT IS THE REASON THE HANDOFF WAS WRONG.** The retroactive keys
were added to quiet the parser while the ruling was outstanding. They made three UNROLLED sessions
look rolled — so #53's handoff instruction *"2f IS 12 BLOCKS DEEP … roll all 12"* was never a
runnable instruction. **It was 9.** A session acting on it without measuring would have hit the
duplicate-key refusal three times and had no account of why. [[assertion-propagation-gap]]:
a claim that was never true is never chased.

#### 2026-07-30 #54
> **pre-flight:** ⛔ **NO BAND PUBLISHED — TWELFTH CONSECUTIVE, but the cause is NAMED this time, not refused.** Dave scoped the window at the opener by **QUOTA** (80% all-model / 82% Fable, ~6h25 to reset), not by fill. ⚠ **Quota is not fill, and neither is throughput** — the three were conflated OUT LOUD this window before being separated. Priced as ONE dense window, no lanes, Fable off the table at 82%.
> **CLOSED: the job Dave picked was runnable; the job the HANDOFF described was not.** *"2f is 12 blocks deep — roll all 12."* It was **9**, and the gap was a hand-patch nobody had ruled. ⇒ the window spent its first third MEASURING the job before doing it, which is the only reason it landed at all.
> **★ THE LESSON — RIGHT ANSWERS BY RECALL ARE INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM WRONG ANSWERS BY RECALL UNTIL ONE IS WRONG.** 2f was reconstructed from `_gm_move.py` and the ledger; `_RUNBOOK-capture-ritual.md` went unread until Dave asked *"does that mean we are in forgetful territory?"*. **Every recalled fact was correct** — 2g last, explicit paths, Desktop closed, dates from `date` — so **no gate, no selftest and no error ledger could have flagged it.** Prior instances (#36 #41 #51) were all caught because recall FAILED and left a defect. **A clean result is not evidence of a sound method**, and this is the first instance where nothing went wrong.
> **★★ THE SECOND LESSON, AND IT IS DAVE'S CATCH: A SELF-CONTRADICTING RUNBOOK DEFEATS "READ THE RUNBOOK".** `_RUNBOOK-context-gauge.md` stated ds-023's stop line correctly at line 110 and **contradicted it in two other sections**; `_RUNBOOK-capture-ritual.md` propagated the wrong half. **Reading the trigger section — the one the ritual itself points at — returned the WRONG rule**, and #54 read it back to Dave in its own wrap note. ⇒ **the recurrence was never a memory failure; canon was handing out both answers.** Eleven sessions. ✅ Reconciled + gated.
> **★ THE THIRD, cheap but sharp:** *a fixture that cannot express the failure will certify the bug.* `roll_2f`'s one-stratum fixture had certified an anchor defect since #34; a SANDWICH fixture — one stratum above, one below — found it in a single run, because each side falsifies a different half of the fix.

That is the discipline the doors exist to serve, reached by a different road.

· measured 2026-08-02 (`measure_tokens` → method `real`). ⛔ **#87'S OWN ARITHMETIC, ATTRIBUTED FIRST: GM 47,712 → 44,890 = -2,822, LS 28,287 → 26,910 = -1,377 — the #87 banner/stratum/delta IN, the #83 banner + #84 stratum + #82 delta rolled OUT, both hand-patches removed.** ★ A banner is a SWAP, not an ADD — these figures were measured AFTER the regen, on the artefact. ⛔ **#84'S OWN ARITHMETIC, ATTRIBUTED FIRST: GM 45,236 → 47,712 = +2,476, MINE. *Per the capture-review-decisions rule: rulings + WHY, so feedback doesn't evaporate.
Lane record: `_LIVE-STATE.md` §🔀 → scope v2 → scope v1 → the record note (all 2026-07-26).
Underscore-prefixed = exempt from `_capture_gate.py`'s glob by design (it IS the ledger).
All nodes seeded `unaudited` per `_RUNBOOK-decision-audit.md` — nothing self-promotes.*

| # | Ruling (Dave, 2026-07-26, via explicit option-select in-session) | Why (from the scope notes) | Audit |
|---|---|---|---|
| **D1** | **(a) Repo-side only.** Blocking gate bites on notes/dossiers; memory files carry the same fields by ritual discipline, session-checked at step 3, honestly UNENFORCED. | The store is invisible to every gate (runbook step 3, verified against sandbox mounts); per the gate-glob-scope rule a claim wider than the glob is a false inscription. | unaudited |
| **D2** | **Five status values:** `observed \| inferred \| ruled \| floated \| standing`. | The worked example (two-hemispheres essay — long-lived, Dave-owned, neither floated nor ruled) demanded the fifth register; four values would flatten it (memento-three-registers: never flatten). | unaudited |
| **D3** | **One script** — `_capture_gate.py` finally built, provenance checks inside it. | Less plumbing; the capture-ritual runbook already owned the spec (§ "The gate"). | unaudited |
| **D4′** | **Sequence §4.1 → A (Cowork) → C (Copilot) → B (Claude Code).** Supersedes v1's D4 row (which lacked C). | A proves the loop cheapest; C tests the harness-spinoff portability thesis + audits the capture ritual repo-only; B awaits Dave's CC migration. Flips freely if he moves sooner. | unaudited |
| **D5** | **RULED via A-D3 at first shape build:** dreamer home `.claude/agents/dreamer.md` — enacted. | Single file readable by Claude Code AND VS Code natively. Confirmed at first shape build, exactly as pencilled. | unaudited |
| D6 | *Pencilled, Dave's own action:* one-time check — repo on GitHub (private), Copilot tier, cloud-agent automations enabled. Before any Shape C build. | Shape C precondition (scope v2 §1.2). | — |
| **A-D1** | **Manual first, schedule later.** First dream pass runs by hand in the Shape A build session; the recurring task is created only after Dave reads the first proposals file. | Prove-one-then-wave (chart-expansion precedent): automation must earn itself on one proven output. | unaudited |
| **A-D2** | **Weekly, last ~15 transcripts** — the schedule's config once A-D1's proof lands. Not enacted until then. | ~15 ≈ the recent working set; weekly keeps plan usage low and proposals digestible. | unaudited |
| **A-D3** | **Enact D5 now:** dreamer steering spec checked in at `.claude/agents/dreamer.md`; task prompts say "read + follow", never restate. | One versioned spec maintained once (scope v2 §3), serving Shape A today and B/C from the same file. | unaudited |
| **A-D4** | **Proposals at `notes/_dream/YYYY-MM-DD-proposals.md`**, carrying `provenance:` + `status: floated` by discipline; `_dream/` stays OUTSIDE the gate glob until it earns its own gate. | Verified in-session: `_capture_gate.py` glob = `notes/*.md` → the subdir is honestly ungated (gate-glob-scope rule); claiming enforcement there would be a false inscription. | unaudited |
| **P1–P8** | **First dream pass RULED (Dave, 2026-07-26, explicit option-select).** P1 archive sibling **accept-enact-now** · P2 commit script **accept-enact-now** · P3 render-runbook fold **accept-enact-now** · P4 count corrections **accept-enact-now** · P5 ds-010 re-surface **accept-enact-now** (tracking line only; the design call stays Dave's) · **P6 DEFER to its own session** (rebuild Half-2 vs re-shape bands — real decision + possible build, not ruled hot; parked in `_FUTURE-STATE.md`) · P7 tuner status correction **accept-enact-now** · P8 sweep **accepted, action Dave's** (host-side rm; optional runbook step added). | 7 of 8 were propagation gaps with known-correct fixes and repo-verified receipts (conductor spot-checked 3/3 exact); P6 alone required choosing between two shapes, so it gets a session, not a hot ruling. Rejected: none — nothing for the next pass to avoid re-floating beyond what's now enacted. | unaudited |
| **S-D1** | **The pass EARNED the schedule** — weekly task created per A-D1/A-D2 (`memento-dream-pass`, Sundays 07:10, last ~15 transcripts, prompt = "read + follow `dreamer.md`", output = proposals file ONLY). | Prove-one-then-wave satisfied: 8 proposals, 3/3 spot-checks exact, 7 of 8 accepted on first read. | unaudited |
| **S-D2** | **Wart 1 fixed: `--wrap --lane` flag** — skips ONLY the GOOD-MORNING header check; the skip prints (never silent); `_LIVE-STATE` check still bites; bite-tested in the selftest. | The lane is now recurring (S-D1), so the reminder-FAIL would be weekly noise; the skip is scoped to exactly the check the lane ruling invalidates (gate-glob-scope logic applied to a flag). | unaudited |

Saved verbatim to `notes/2026-07-26-convergence-anthropic-dreaming.md` + the two field lines (`status: inferred`); capture gate build-mode 0 fail. **Convergence `-v2` UNBLOCKED** — the rewrite itself still owed, its own session. | The blocker was never a decision, only a missing file; the moment the file existed the fix was mechanical. | unaudited |
| **V2-P5(b)** | **ENACTED** — Dave's "love your work continue" immediately after the say-yes-and-it-goes-in ask, read as the yes (interpretation flagged in-session, vetoable). Save-cited-uploads clause added to ritual step 1, with the worked precedent both ways (lamish saved→never blocked; convergence unsaved→blocked ×3). | The clause is one reversible line and Dave had seen it twice; the cost asymmetry (weekly re-ask vs one-word revert) favours enacting. | unaudited |
| **S-D4** | **"Run dream pass" = one phrase (Dave's ask, 2026-07-26 evening).** Conductor sequence inscribed as `knowledge/_RUNBOOK-dream-pass.md` (single source, sibling of `dreamer.md`'s role for the dreamer side); Cowork skill `dream-pass` = thin pointer (read+follow, never restate); weekly task prompt REPLACED with the same thin pointer + non-negotiables + STOP conditions. All three converge on the runbook. | The conductor checklist lived only in chat prompts — the reconstruct-from-memory failure the lane hunts (same WHY as P2's commit script). Read-the-runbook rule applied to the lane itself. | unaudited |

1b/2/3 + gate section amended; cutover note `notes/2026-07-26-provenance-cutover.md`; the three
